# Episode 7 generation memo — capacity-indexed clinical handoff repair

Status: proposed Harbor experiment only. No cohort scan, fitting, adjudication, prospective monitoring, chart review, calibration, decision curve, or result was executed.

Parent: candidate-e8f01f3e9b6fcb61f263c55b. This child preserves the parent’s fixed population, time zero, windows, primary estimand, D_D/D_I/U_T boundary, regime-held-out hypothesis, B0/B1 and SS-Obs alternatives, source bindings, and three inspected abstract-only works. The substantive change is a predeclared, capacity-indexed handoff from retrospective evidence to a future observational monitoring/chart-review study. It does not introduce a treatment claim or an action threshold.

## Scientific boundary and decision question

The strongest evidence-supported claim remains limited: hepatic reserve and post-locoregional decompensation matter clinically [K1], transient TACE injury should be distinguished from clinically meaningful decompensation [K2], and reserve scores/dynamic monitoring are imperfect constructs [K3]. The available HCC release can test whether a day 0–7 trajectory adds internally transportable prognostic information for a discharge-anchored, high-specificity coded endpoint. It cannot establish that the code is true decompensation, validate laboratory units, identify mortality, prove mechanism, or show that monitoring changes care.

The unresolved claim is unchanged:

> In all eligible adults with HCC and a first observed TACE, a day 0–7 laboratory trajectory that adds held-out prognostic information beyond time-zero baseline will retain direction and calibration across later calendar bands, departments and observed assay/name/sample-type regimes, without the gain being explained by endpoint-document discordance or observation intensity.

The new decision question is narrower and operational: if this retrospective signal survives the locked transportability and endpoint-validity gates, is there enough capacity-indexed, blinded adjudication yield to justify a prospective observational monitoring/chart-review pilot? A supportive handoff authorizes study planning only. It does not authorize an alert, a monitoring schedule as clinical care, a treatment change, or a patient-level risk threshold.

## Fixed population, time, estimand, and timing boundary

Use the unchanged all-eligible adult first-observed-TACE HCC population:

- Select the earliest procedure whose procedures.手术 contains TACE, 肝动脉化疗栓塞, 经导管肝动脉栓塞 or 动脉化疗栓塞, with parseable procedures.开始时间 and a matching HCC encounter.
- Require encounters.年龄 >=18 and HCC diagnosis (肝细胞癌 or 肝恶性肿瘤) on or before the index encounter through the within-HCC composite key (患者主索引, 就诊号).
- Exclude a pre-index high-specificity decompensation term from the unchanged list (腹水, 肝性脑病, 消化道出血, 食管胃底静脉曲张, 肝肾综合征, 急性肝衰竭, 肝功能衰竭, 自发性腹膜炎, 黄疸). Because diagnoses has no time field, the linked encounter time is only a proxy and same-encounter ambiguity remains.
- Time zero is procedures.开始时间. Keep procedures.结束时间 and procedures.手术来源 for audit only; infer neither dose nor treated territory.
- Baseline is the closest assay-specific numeric labs.定量结果 in [-14,0] days. Dynamic observations are raw labs in [0,7] days. Preserve lab names, qualitative/numeric results, sample types and 检验时间. There is no units column; do not compute unit-dependent ALBI, MELD, Child-Pugh or cross-assay thresholds.
- Primary D_D is the first distinct encounter with admission in index days 8–90, after the observable index discharge, and a linked high-specificity diagnosis component. Missing discharge is a separate ascertainment stratum.
- D_I is the index-anchored sensitivity: the first distinct qualifying encounter in days 8–90 regardless of observable discharge.
- U_T is a continued-index or no-distinct-anchor candidate. Never assign an invented date, turn U_T into an event, or interpret it as death.
- Report composite, ascites, encephalopathy, bleeding, renal/hepatic failure and jaundice separately. No mortality, hospice, terminal competing-risk or death-date claim is available.

The primary estimand remains: among adults with HCC and a first observed TACE, does the day 0–7 trajectory add held-out prognostic information beyond baseline for new high-specificity decompensation-coded admission during days 8–90 after index discharge?

## Chronology-frozen models and transportability

Freeze all definitions before outcome inspection. Calendar split is train 2010-07-27–2018-12-31, validation 2019-01-01–2021-12-31, untouched test 2022-01-01–2025-10-03, recomputed from the verified source maximum if required. Report full test and predeclared 2022–2023 and 2024–2025-10-03 bands without tuning on either. No patient crosses a split.

Department regime is raw index encounters.就诊科室, including missing. Assay regime is the exact train-observed (labs.检验, labs.样本类型) pair for the predeclared panel: bilirubin, albumin, platelets, PT/INR or PT ratio, creatinine, sodium, AST, ALT and AFP only if present, with unseen-in-train explicit. This is an observation regime, not evidence of unit equivalence.

B0/B1 remain equally specific:

- B0: age, sex, index department, HCC/cirrhosis/portal-vein-thrombus/prior-decompensation flags, procedure context, pre-index utilization, assay-specific baseline values and baseline missingness.
- B1: B0 plus, for exactly the same assay/name/sample-type inputs, baseline, last value, change from baseline, within-window minimum/maximum, count, last-observation day and missingness over [0,7]. Use train-only preprocessing and dictionaries.
- Fit L2 logistic models for D_D and regularized cause-specific survival forms for D_I; train, validation-tune, then predict untouched test.

SS-Obs remains equally specific: a two-factor irregular-time state-space model using the same B0 variables and raw [0,7] observations as B1, with train-fitted assay-regime measurement error, irregular timestamps, missingness indicators and partial pooling. One factor represents a slowly varying reserve representation and one transient injury; a day-7 state head predicts D_D and a cause-specific hazard head predicts D_I. Observation heads model timing/counts and early-care encounters, without post-day-7 or endpoint text. Report state uncertainty and convergence. Its purpose is to test whether ordered observations separate persistent coordinated change, transient injury and observation intensity; it is not a mechanistic claim.

Compare B0, B1 and SS-Obs on the same chronological test patients: paired Brier score, calibration intercept/slope, discrimination, time-dependent/IPCW metrics for D_I, exploratory DCA on a fixed mathematical risk grid, regime contrasts, 2,000-patient bootstrap or a bounded prespecified equivalent, and leakage audit. Include timestamp permutation, pre-index pseudo-trajectory, counts/lags/departments/calendar-only, discharge-lag and early-care process models, component blocks, and missing-discharge/early-care/document-concordance contrasts.

Supportive transportability requires the trajectory increment to retain favorable direction globally and in every adequately supported regime (at least 100 patients and 20 adjudication-independent computable events where applicable), with no material calibration deterioration and no gain explained by observation count/process or endpoint discordance. Adverse means a supported reversal, disappearance after endpoint/observation controls, confinement to discharge/early-care strata, or loss under index anchoring. Inconclusive means sparse support, unstable weights, convergence failure, unresolved assay units, large U_T/text-insufficient fractions or inadequate adjudication agreement. These categories concern an observed-data prognostic claim, not causality.

## Endpoint adjudication and capacity-indexed prospective handoff

### Retrospective adjudication-first gate

Before reading fitted test predictions, define endpoint strata and draw the adjudication sample. The packet contains only the index procedure/encounter context, index and follow-up admission/discharge fields, raw diagnoses, relevant clinical-document fields, raw labs and bounded medications, examinations and orders used to describe care intensity. It contains no model score, prediction, threshold, B0/B1/SS-Obs label, or post-hoc model stratum. Reviewers are blinded to model and baseline-versus-trajectory status.

Two clinicians independently label each packet; a third resolves disagreement. Labels are: definite new/worsening decompensation; probable but date-uncertain decompensation; pre-existing disease; isolated TACE injury/post-embolization syndrome; competing illness or HCC progression; planned/unclear; no support; text insufficient; and terminal event/date only if explicitly date-qualified. Planned status is unknown unless the packet states it. A date-uncertain label cannot manufacture D_D or D_I.

Report design-weighted component PPV, negative agreement, weighted timing-uncertain/text-insufficient fractions, inter-rater and final agreement, diagnosis/document discordance and regime-specific validity. This sample validates an endpoint in sampled records; it cannot make a code population-wide gold standard.

### Handoff population and queue construction

The handoff is a future observational pilot protocol, not an executed prospective result. It begins only after the retrospective cohort ledger, model objects, feature manifest, leakage audit and endpoint gate are locked.

For each future all-eligible index, create a day-7 queue entry using only information allowed by the fixed experiment: B0 data and the [0,7] B1/SS-Obs inputs. Freeze B1 and SS-Obs weights and preprocessing before queue construction. Define the primary locked composite rank as the mean of the within-batch percentile ranks of B1 and SS-Obs D_D risk; if SS-Obs is unavailable because of its predeclared convergence/availability rule, use the B1 percentile rank and mark the fallback. Define rank disagreement as the absolute difference between the two available percentile ranks. At day 7, queue records by the locked B1 risk, the locked SS-Obs risk, the composite rank and rank disagreement. A reviewer sees only a blinded packet identifier and source chart packet, never score, rank, model identity, or queue assignment. The queue does not trigger treatment.

Use one predeclared annual capacity tier as primary and two sensitivity tiers:

- C=240 unique packets/year (low capacity), C=480 (primary), and C=720 (high capacity), with two independent clinician reviews per packet and a third review only for disagreement. Capacity means unique packets, not reviewer encounters; the actual completed count and reviewer-hours are reported.
- Within each capacity, allocate 60% to a representative random queue, 25% to a rank-enriched queue, and 15% to a process/disagreement queue. The prospective frame is allocated across four day-7-observable cells formed by discharge observed by day 7 (yes/no) and early-care encounter during days 0–7 (yes/no); a missing-data cell is added only if the locked feature-availability rule requires it. Index department and calendar band are recorded for later regime contrasts, not used as post-outcome eligibility. These cells are frozen before review and collapsed only when a cell count is below 5.
- The representative queue uses simple random sampling without replacement within cell. The rank-enriched queue uses randomized probability-proportional-to-size sampling without replacement within cell with size 1/(1+locked-rank) for the locked B1/SS-Obs composite rank; every eligible record retains nonzero inclusion probability. The process/disagreement queue samples with known probabilities proportional to predeclared early-care, discharge-missingness and B1-versus-SS-Obs rank-disagreement indicators, with a uniform positive floor. No queue is selected using D_D, D_I, U_T, document status, adjudication labels or any information after day 7.
- The exact random seed, queue type, cell, frame size N_h, draw size n_h and first-order inclusion probability π_i are frozen in a sampling manifest before unblinding. If draws overlap, use the prespecified union inclusion probability π_i = 1 - product_q(1-π_iq) and retain the queue indicators. The analysis weight is w_i=1/π_i, normalized within each target stratum only for descriptive rates. The capacity queue’s weighted yield and the representative queue’s population prevalence are not conflated.
- For any capacity k in {120, 240, 480, 720}, estimate the weighted definite-or-probable yield among the first k records in the locked ranked queue, with Hájek weighted PPV and design-based 95% confidence intervals using Taylor linearization or 2,000 design-respecting replicate samples. Also report weighted sensitivity/recall, timing-uncertain fraction, reviewer agreement and effective sample size. These are estimates of review yield, not clinical benefit.
- The primary handoff contrast is the weighted yield in the locked rank-enriched queue at C=480 versus its matched representative random queue, with the same packet review protocol. Report absolute yield difference, enrichment ratio, and 95% uncertainty. A queue is not clinically useful merely because it has a high code rate; the endpoint-validity label and disagreement must be shown.

The same blinded chart-review packet is adjudicated after the complete days 8–90 record is available. Prospective monitoring observations may be recorded at day 7, but reviewers adjudicating the outcome remain blinded to scores, ranks, queue type and any monitoring decision. For the retrospective endpoint-validity experiment only, outcome-known strata (D_D/D_I/U_T, document concordance and timing uncertainty) may be used to improve precision, with their separate inverse-probability weights; those labels are never used to construct the future day-7 queue. No reviewer is asked to infer an action threshold. A future pilot must obtain local clinical governance approval and define privacy, consent/waiver, reviewer qualification and escalation procedures; none is available in this retrospective release.

### Handoff decision criteria

These are predeclared go/no-go criteria for an observational monitoring/chart-review study, not treatment criteria.

- Supportive: the retrospective trajectory increment passes the global and adequately supported regime-held-out gates; blinded adjudication has clinician-judged acceptable agreement and no material regime-specific validity failure; the primary C=480 rank-enriched queue has a positive weighted yield difference versus the matched representative queue with a 95% interval excluding zero, effective sample size at least 50 in each primary queue, and no adverse direction in either C=240 or C=720; timing-uncertain/text-insufficient labels are reported and do not drive the result. This supports funding a prospective observational pilot to measure feasibility, adjudicated yield, reviewer burden and calibration. It supports no alert or treatment.
- Adverse: the ranked queue is no better than or worse than the capacity-matched representative queue, the yield advantage disappears after endpoint adjudication, a supported regime reverses, reviewer disagreement or timing uncertainty is concentrated in the queue, or benefit is reproduced by timestamp/pre-index/count-only controls. The monitoring direction should be revised or abandoned; no prospective action rule is justified.
- Inconclusive: a capacity tier cannot be filled, effective sample size is below 50, inclusion probabilities or queue frame are not recoverable, weighted intervals are unstable, the clinician panel cannot judge endpoint validity, assay units remain unresolved, or the primary interval includes both a meaningful benefit and harm. Continue only by revising the endpoint/registry or collecting the missing evidence; do not interpret this as a null.
- Even a supportive handoff cannot establish mortality benefit, causal effect, clinical mechanism, external transportability, prospective benefit, or a safe patient-level threshold. Those require independent clinical adjudication, unit verification, governance review and a new prospective study.

### Decision-curve boundary

DCA remains exploratory on D_D over a fixed mathematical risk grid with treat-none and treat-all references, and only after the adjudication packet is complete. It cannot choose a clinical threshold. If the endpoint is not clinically adjudication-supported, DCA is labelled non-actionable. No treatment or monitoring recommendation is produced.

# Context-specific MerTK target prioritization in rheumatoid-arthritis synovial coculture

Status: Lead design, planned experiment; no scientific screening result has been executed. Episode 1, crossover of D2-T1 and D2-T2.

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The available evidence supports two facts but leaves an actionable boundary unresolved. MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states are associated with remission and can induce a fibroblast repair response; the inspected source also reports that MerTK inhibition increases FLS IL6 and MMP1/3/14 [K1]. Separately, HBEGF-positive macrophages can drive an invasive FLS program [K2], and fibroblast pathology is heterogeneous across immune-interacting and vascular-interacting states [K3]. These findings do not establish that MerTK perturbation has the same consequence in every macrophage context, nor that a MerTK-directed intervention should be selected without stratifying protective versus inflammatory macrophage states.

Falsifiable hypothesis: in rheumatoid-arthritis synovial FLS coculture, MerTK inhibition produces a larger inflammatory FLS response when the macrophage context is MerTK/CD206-positive (resolution-like) than when it is MerTK/CD206-negative, after accounting for contributing FLS/macrophage donors and generic LPS stimulation. The clinically consequential extension is that a MerTK-preservation or activation strategy should be considered state-stratified: patients or cocultures enriched for the MerTK-positive/CD206-positive resolution context should show the greatest avoidable fibroblast harm from MerTK loss. This is a hypothesis about a perturbation-by-context interaction, not a claim that MerTK activation is already an effective treatment.

The strongest available claim is a broad protective association/perturbational effect, not clinical efficacy or direct target causality. The strongest rival is that the observed FLS changes are generic inflammatory or stress responses, cell-composition/sorting proxies, donor/reuse artifacts, or assay timing effects; under that rival, inhibitor effects should not show a reproducible CD206-context interaction after donor-aware adjustment. [K2] makes the macrophage-state alternative consequential, while [K3] motivates separating FLS state readouts from mere bulk expression changes. The proposed advance over [K1] is a state-by-perturbation safety/selection test, not another broad MerTK expression association.

## Population, boundaries, and exact data bindings

Primary population: all 33 recorded pseudobulk FLS samples in the prepared E-MTAB-8873 matrix, restricted to samples whose design row has cell_type=type B synovial cell, tissue=synovial membrane, and a documented co-culture condition. Primary contrasts are macrophages pre-treated with MerTK inhibitor versus no treatment within condition=co-cultured with MerTK/CD206pos macrophages and, as the context comparator, the corresponding CD206neg condition. No raw cell is treated as an independent donor.

Required primary inputs and keys:

- [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.counts.tsv.gz (catalog SHA-256 d218d3c46b652d533673c9ffc7876585bc51a39371f036e92d3ce568f28a4c0f): table with feature row key and 33 sample-ID columns. Verified measured feature columns include MERTK|NM_006343.2|Reference_end, MRC1|NM_002438.3|Reference_end, TREM2|NM_018965.3|Reference_end, SPP1|NM_000582.2|Reference_end, IL1B|NM_000576.2|Reference_end, IL6|NM_000600.4|Reference_end, MMP1|NM_002421.3|Reference_end, MMP3|NM_002422.4|Reference_end, MMP12|NM_002426.5|Reference_end, MMP13|NM_002427.3|Reference_end, and MMP14|NM_004995.3|Reference_end.
- [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.design.json (SHA-256 fd2ae05bd0e31a8ba72454b97e22a48f5e53c179370e5f4b5343f5382b217ae4): one row per matrix column with required fields sample_id, donor_id, donor_status, age, sex, tissue, cell_type, condition, treatment, source_metadata, and cells. Join design.sample_id to the matrix header exactly. Parse the comma-separated contributing IDs in donor_id as separate FLS/macrophage random-effect memberships; do not silently repair the malformed/ambiguous R1_SA256A_FLS_SA260R_Mpos label.
- [private-path]/assay-registry.json (SHA-256 e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f): registry table documenting 33 samples, 445 measured features, no verified single donors, and the explicit prohibition on ordinary donor t-tests.
- Audit lineage/source members, read-only and not treated as independent replicates: E-MTAB-8873/E-MTAB-8873.sdrf.txt (SHA-256 4e564426bb68e05d93e997a9124d42f252a19680abfe54315676893ae479f719) plus the registered R1/R2/R5 R*_SA*_..._RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz members listed in datasets/therapeutic_targets/metadata.json; inhibitor members include R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_Inhibitor, R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor, R1_SA256A_FLS_SA260R_Mpos_Inhibitor, R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos_preInhibitor, and R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos_preInhibitor. The prepared pseudobulk table is the analysis table; individual cells are not additional independent observations.

The primary design has five inhibitor-treated samples (one CD206neg and four CD206pos) and 23 untreated samples, plus LPS-treated context controls and six FLS-only samples. This sparsity is itself a falsification/deferral condition: a state interaction can be estimated only as exploratory with uncertainty and donor-cluster sensitivity, not as a definitive clinical effect.

Secondary context inputs, never joined by matching patient IDs:

- E-MTAB-8316 prepared matrix [private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.counts.tsv.gz (SHA-256 9ceb4b7cf3d52d7f6e3800c827d491b174b646826fae9c6d1433c5d64b219645) and design [private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.design.json (SHA-256 ca011580853bbea30b4f68f21bb5b017721c3e47bfefee6e9083b44da04c4c81). Its 12 columns are MK11/MK12, MK15/MK16, MK19/MK20, MK23/MK24, MK3/MK4 and MK7/MK8: six verified within-other_donor_id none versus UNC106238 pairs nested in four verified donor IDs (SA114, SA051, SA104, SA049). Use only as a paired exploratory perturbation/state check after reconciling its monocyte labels and protocol readout; do not claim twelve independent donors or FLS-specific effects. No time field is present.
- E-MTAB-8322 prepared matrix [private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz (SHA-256 95bc3a964f3fbc57cde1957ec6637aaac806cedd8dfccc0526158e9068f43f36) and design [private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.design.json (SHA-256 4ef38a7031542ec07551d585e9a2218f2620320018b3d56a86bde5a0b672a3da). It has 27 macrophage pseudobulk columns across healthy (4), treatment-naive RA (6), remission (7), resistant RA (6), and undifferentiated arthritis (4); exclude SA149P and UPASA149 from independent-donor inference. Its matrix uses Ensembl feature IDs and no configured feature-map file, so target-module/state scoring is blocked pending a named, frozen human annotation release. Use design-state metadata descriptively and do not call cross-sectional groups transitions.
- GSE95588 prepared coculture matrices and designs are available, but donor-to-GSM mapping is unresolved and the coculture branch includes earlier GSE57723 material. It is retained as an exploratory/rival context only; no donor-aware inferential claim or independent validation will use it.

There are no longitudinal time fields or patient treatment transitions in these molecular tables. treatment, condition, and source metadata are assay conditions, not clinical time. No source namespace is joined across assays.

## Computable Harbor experiment

1. Freeze the eligible E-MTAB-8873 rows and an analysis manifest recording the exact filtering above, sample IDs, donor memberships, and all excluded/ambiguous rows. Normalize each sample's measured feature counts to log2(CPM + pseudocount), using the matrix's feature and sample columns; do not merge duplicate identifiers or infer absent genes.
2. Prespecify two outcomes. The primary harm score is the mean of z-scored IL6, MMP1, MMP3 and MMP14 across measured features; secondary harm components are IL1B, MMP12 and MMP13. The context/state panel is MERTK, MRC1, TREM2 and SPP1. If a planned repair marker is not present in the exact header, it is unavailable rather than imputed.
3. Fit the simple baseline: feature-wise and harm-score linear models with inhibitor, macrophage context (CD206pos/neg), inhibitor-by-context interaction, LPS indicator, FLS-only indicator, age, and assay batch/round when identifiable. Use cross-classified donor-cluster random intercepts or cluster-robust inference for every contributing donor; average repeated context measurements only when the documented donor/condition definition warrants it. Generate donor-cluster bootstrap intervals and leave-one-donor-cluster-out sensitivity, not ordinary donor t-tests. The estimand is the inhibitor contrast within context and their difference, on the FLS harm score.
4. Fit a substantive mechanistic alternative on exactly the same inputs: a hierarchical multivariate latent-state model in which a macrophage-resolution score is a weighted latent factor of MERTK/MRC1/TREM2 (with SPP1 and IL1B as an inflammatory contrast) and FLS harm is a latent factor of IL6/MMP1/MMP3/MMP14. Estimate the inhibitor-by-context interaction jointly with crossed FLS and macrophage donor effects, allowing feature-specific residual covariance. The model's target is not a predictive label; it is the posterior distribution of the context-specific perturbation effect and the probability that the interaction exceeds a prespecified scientifically meaningful direction. Fit by CPU using a reproducible Bayesian or penalized-likelihood implementation; no GPU is needed for this small table. If the donor design is too sparse to identify the latent model, defer it and report the baseline only.
5. Compare the baseline and mechanistic alternative on scientific information: sign and uncertainty of the same interaction estimand, leave-one-donor-cluster-out stability, posterior/cluster-bootstrap predictive checks, and whether the alternative changes interpretation by separating a correlated macrophage state from the FLS harm outcome. Do not rank by small predictive improvement. No random train/test split is appropriate for this finite hypothesis test; the held-out unit is a donor cluster. The future solver must report coefficient/effect tables, donor membership and exclusions, uncertainty intervals or posterior intervals, feature-level and score-level outputs, sensitivity analyses, and diagnostic plots/data.
6. Compute a bounded negative control: the LPS-treated versus untreated contrast within the same macrophage context where present. A selective MerTK interaction should not be reproduced identically by the LPS contrast. FLS-only samples assess whether an apparent response is present without macrophages; this is a control, not evidence of direct MerTK action.
7. Contextualize, do not pool, E-MTAB-8316 paired UNC106238 versus none at the verified donor/other-donor unit and E-MTAB-8322 condition proportions/state metadata. A consistent direction can motivate a balanced follow-up, but it cannot be called external validation because the datasets derive from the same literature program and have different biological units.

Supportive result: the inhibitor-by-context interaction is positive and materially larger in CD206pos coculture for the prespecified harm score, stable in donor-cluster sensitivity, while LPS and FLS-only controls do not reproduce it. This supports state-stratified MerTK preservation/activation as a next target-development experiment, not a clinical treatment claim.

Adverse result: no interaction, a larger CD206neg effect, the same signal under LPS, or a signal confined to FLS-only samples. This refutes the proposed selectivity claim and favors generic inflammatory/cell-composition explanations; do not prioritize MerTK state targeting on this evidence.

Inconclusive result: sparse inhibitor cells, unresolved contributing-donor mappings, nonidentifiable latent model, contradictory donor clusters, or missing annotation/feature coverage. Acquire balanced paired Mpos/Mneg cocultures with matched FLS and macrophage donors, inhibitor dose/viability data, MerTK protein/activation and efferocytosis readouts, secreted mediators, and direct FLS invasion/matrix degradation. Clinical treatment benefit, patient selection, and mechanism require expert review, orthogonal perturbation (e.g., agonism or genetic perturbation), and an independent cohort; Harbor QA can check computation and whether conclusions follow from outputs but cannot establish those claims.

## Alternative methods and selection

The pathway/paired-score baseline is transparent and appropriate to the sparse, repeated-donor table. The hierarchical multivariate latent-state alternative could reveal whether the apparent interaction is a shared macrophage-to-FLS program rather than a single-gene artifact, and it propagates uncertainty across correlated markers; that information is lost by the baseline. It is deferred as secondary because five inhibitor-treated samples and unresolved contributing-donor structure may not identify crossed latent effects. Both methods use the same exact inputs, estimand, donor-cluster held-out sensitivity and uncertainty outputs. A CPU future solver envelope of 16 CPUs/262144 MiB and 8 GPUs is available in inputs.json, but this study is small and does not justify GPU; the discovery diagnostic jobs completed in under a second, while full solver fit time is unmeasured and should be budgeted as a bounded CPU job. No neural model is required because the scientific uncertainty is mechanistic interaction/selectivity, not prediction.

## What must be newly fitted and completion deliverable

The solver must newly fit the context-by-MerTK-inhibitor effect and its uncertainty from E-MTAB-8873, fit or explicitly defer the hierarchical latent alternative, and produce the frozen analysis manifest, donor-aware effect/uncertainty tables, prespecified harm/state scores, LPS/FLS-only controls, leave-one-donor-cluster-out results, and a conclusion linked to those computed outputs. Completion is not a polished hypothesis or a readiness probe: it requires these computed outputs and an interpretation that distinguishes supportive, adverse and inconclusive cases.

## Evidence and prior-work mapping

[K1] establishes the broad MerTK-positive resolution/repair claim and the reported inhibitor FLS response; the proposed state-specific interaction and donor-aware target-selection test are new relative to that inspected work.
[K2] supplies the strongest biological rival: inflammatory macrophage state can drive fibroblast pathology independently of the proposed MerTK-selective explanation.
[K3] bounds the fibroblast outcome interpretation by showing that inflammatory FLS states are heterogeneous and niche-linked; the proposal therefore prespecifies multiple measured FLS outputs and does not treat one marker as mechanism.

Key references and attached inspected excerpts are in work/lead/key-references.json and work/lead/evidence/.

## Demonstration and seed dispositions

- D2-T1 retained: context-specific intervention response becomes the inhibitor-by-CD206 context interaction, with direct-target claims explicitly deferred.
- D2-T2 retained: benefit versus harm is operationalized as FLS inflammatory harm plus preservation of the resolution-like macrophage context.
- Natural-history transformer demonstration: not pursued as a molecular topic; its lesson is to distinguish observed structured histories from a proposed learned representation. It adds no necessary information to this small assay.
- Cancer multimodal demonstration: full text and images are unavailable and the configured molecular sources contain no imaging/longitudinal oncology outcomes; no adaptation is scientifically grounded here.
- Bayesian longitudinal EHR demonstration: genetics/EHR trajectory inputs are absent and the molecular question is better resolved by donor-aware mechanistic contrasts; no EHR adaptation is claimed.

## Explicit unavailable evidence

The configured data do not provide clinical outcomes, medication response for the coculture donors, MerTK agonism/genetic loss-of-function, protein/phosphorylation/efferocytosis measurements, viability, secreted protein, dose-response/time-course, spatial localization, or an independent validation cohort. Expression and pseudobulk cell-state contrasts cannot establish a clinical benefit, a direct molecular mechanism, or a safe therapeutic window.

- Source lineage members include `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.sdrf.txt` (SHA-256 `4e564426bb68e05d93e997a9124d42f252a19680abfe54315676893ae479f719`) and the registered RSEC members used by the primary rows: `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_Inhibitor_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz` (SHA-256 `ef435ca4a16bb535f74ad077297861f2f9672827c2d2a4e7f9e65171bea2b0d7`), `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz` (`1dafc0a646fc9cdc1101803cf9d36802a1775844a85877930341ebe6edcf2176`), `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz` (`144b62d01db3f4635bdd19ecc599ce7670770ddf79b7e72e846c46a3cf732e9e`), `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz` (`e3d6554a4e6c262fca98ce8263fb3c1d86d2c47c5f7e3e1fe5aa516367b3f599`), and the R2/R5 `Mpos_preInhibitor` members (`e14006cefdb3b642c3f280d3e888b3e16767e2b36288bb7029ce2e52d36c6a85` and `09bb1e81c247f251930c10ea8bfc25e651c01a8746a2fbe630d27dce4cb064a8`). These archive members are lineage, not additional observations.

Eligible primary rows have `tissue=synovial membrane`, `cell_type=type B synovial cell`, and a co-culture condition. The exact exposure rows are R1 `SA259A_Mneg_Inhibitor`, R1 `SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor), and R1 `SA260R_Mpos_Inhibitor). R2 and R5 `Mpos_preInhibitor` are a separate secondary tier; protocol equivalence must be established before any sensitivity use. Mixed 1Mpos/3Mneg and 3Mpos/1Mneg rows are composition controls, not clean context labels. FLS-only and not-co-cultured rows are controls, not primary cocultures. The R1 `SA260R_Mpos` untreated row has conflicting donor metadata and is sensitivity-only. There are no clinical time points: the temporal boundary is the single recorded assay condition; no longitudinal or treatment-transition claim is allowed.

Secondary E-MTAB-8316:

- Counts table: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.counts.tsv.gz`, SHA-256 `9ceb4b7cf3d52d7f6e3800c827d491b174b646826fae9c6d1433c5d64b219645`. It has 12 sample columns `MK11,MK12,MK15,MK16,MK19,MK20,MK23,MK24,MK3,MK4,MK7,MK8` and 58,302 Ensembl feature rows; the feature field contains Ensembl IDs, not the 8873 transcript labels.
- Design table: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.design.json`, SHA-256 `ca011580853bbea30b4f68f21bb5b017721c3e47bfefee6e9083b44da04c4c81`. Required fields are `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `other_donor_id`, `donor_status`, `condition`, `treatment`, `source_metadata`, `tissue), `cell_type`, `age), and `sex), plus `unit_definition`. The six exact same-unit pairs are MK11/MK12, MK15/MK16, MK19/MK20, MK23/MK24, MK3/MK4, and MK7/MK8: within each pair `condition/treatment=none` versus `UNC106238`. They are nested in four verified FLS donor clusters `SA114, SA051, SA104, SA049`; `other_donor_id` identifies six nested monocyte donors `1533,1534,1601,1602,1462,1463`. The registry defines the unit as “FLS donor cluster; monocyte donors nested and balanced across compound conditions.” There is no time field.
- Source lineage members are `[private-path]/MK_readcountMatrix.txt.gz` (SHA-256 `510b69e449ed424adfbf225b8eeaf9faff1f8a973c76951612caf7ae69103228`) and `E-MTAB-8316.sdrf.txt` (SHA-256 `3e304fc612102181c9106532d42b010554f342b8529f6542c04169e50093ce74`). The registry records four verified single donor IDs, six nested monocyte donors, 12 samples, and no 12-independent-donor claim.

No identifier is joined across assays. In particular, SA114/SA049/SA104/SA051 in 8316 are not matched to SA256A, SA259A, SA266A or any other 8873 label. A source comparison may use only separately estimated, explicitly standardized effect summaries after compatibility checks; it may not pool rows, donors, feature IDs or raw counts.

## Estimands and identifiability gates

Normalize each source separately to log2(CPM + 1), preserving original feature IDs and never imputing absent genes.

Primary E-MTAB-8873 outcome:
`H_s` is the mean of feature-standardized IL6, MMP1, MMP3 and MMP14. Standardization parameters are frozen using eligible untreated, unambiguous co-culture reference rows. The primary estimand is

`Delta = [E(H | exact inhibitor, Mpos) - E(H | untreated, Mpos)] - [E(H | exact inhibitor, Mneg) - E(H | untreated, Mneg)]`.

The solver must emit a pre-fit gate with treatment/context cell counts, exact counterpart availability, donor-membership incidence rank, and estimability of the interaction. The gate fails if the model requires the ambiguous mixed rows, the preInhibitor tier, the metadata-conflicted untreated row, a random row split, or independent-donor assumptions. Given the verified design, only the R1 SA256A/SA259A pair supplies a complete same-membership exact-inhibitor Mpos/Mneg contrast; therefore a population-level causal interaction is not automatically identified. A failed or rank-deficient gate returns inconclusive, never a zero estimate.

The baseline is a transparent paired score/interaction analysis: calculate within-membership matched differences wherever explicitly supported, fit context, exposure and interaction with assay round only when rank permits, and represent FLS/macrophage memberships by an incidence matrix. Use cluster bootstrap or a bounded sign/permutation sensitivity over contributing membership clusters, leave-one-round-out and leave-one-membership-out analyses. Report H, each component, exact versus preInhibitor tiers, mapping scenarios, and controls. Ordinary donor t-tests and cell-level replication are prohibited.

The E-MTAB-8316 secondary estimand is source-specific:
`d_{f,m,g}=logCPM(UNC106238)_{f,m,g}-logCPM(none)_{f,m,g}`, for each of the six exact pairs, summarized within the four FLS donor clusters with monocyte donor nested dependence. It is not H, not Delta, and not an FLS outcome. A six-pair response can be reported only as exploratory paired evidence; it is not six independent donors.

The 8316 compatibility gate requires: (1) protocol/registry confirmation that UNC106238 is the intended perturbation and that the none/UNC106238 rows are paired units; (2) a named frozen Ensembl-to-gene annotation map if gene-level MERTK/MRC1/TREM2/SPP1 or inflammatory-marker claims are attempted; (3) verified correspondence of cell type and readout to the intended secondary question; and (4) no cross-source donor join. The currently inspected prepared files pass the pairing and donor-nesting checks but fail the configured feature-map requirement for gene-level target claims and do not expose an Mpos/Mneg context. The correct current plan is therefore bounded source-specific triangulation with an explicit non-pooling status, not a hierarchical cross-cohort Delta.

A shared hierarchical cross-cohort effect is scientifically identifiable only if both sources share a measured endpoint, intervention definition, context contrast, feature namespace/annotation and biological unit. They currently do not: 8873 measures targeted FLS coculture harm with transcript labels, while 8316 measures Ensembl-indexed monocyte samples under none/UNC106238 and has no context field. A model with source-specific intercepts cannot repair a missing common estimand. If a future named annotation and protocol adjudication make a common secondary signature defensible, fit source-specific effects with a hierarchical shrinkage sensitivity, never a forced pooled primary coefficient. Otherwise report non-pooling.

## Baseline versus substantive alternative

Both methods use the same source-specific normalized matrices, design fields, paired units and frozen manifests.

The baseline estimates the primary Delta transparently and the 8316 paired d contrasts without a learned prediction target. Its strength is auditable behavior under sparsity; it loses correlated marker structure and can be noisy when one membership drives a contrast.

The alternative is a source-stratified cross-classified multivariate model. For 8873, jointly model IL6/MMP1/MMP3/MMP14 with feature-specific exposure, context and interaction effects, crossed FLS/macrophage membership effects, and a shared harm factor; retain IL1B/MMP12/MMP13 and MERTK/MRC1/TREM2/SPP1 as contrasts. For 8316, fit a multivariate paired response only after the feature-map and protocol gates pass, with FLS-cluster and nested monocyte effects. The target is the same Delta (8873) and source-specific d-vector (8316), not a disease label. Compare signs, uncertainty, marker coherence and leave-cluster-out stability, not predictive accuracy. The alternative can reveal whether a response is a correlated program and whether partial pooling appropriately widens or shrinks uncertainty; the baseline loses that structure.

Do not fit the alternative if the 8873 rank gate fails or the 8316 feature map/units remain unresolved. This is a scientific deferral, not a mechanical simplification. Expected solver resources are 4–8 CPU cores, <16 GiB memory and minutes for the 33-by-11 primary feature table plus 12-by-feature paired secondary table; the estimate is unmeasured and must be bounded in the solver job. GPU is deferred because the bottleneck is identifiability and biological-unit compatibility, not matrix scale. A neural predictor is not selected: a predictive gain cannot distinguish context selectivity from donor/assay confounding and has no clinically meaningful target estimand here.

## Falsification and interpretation

Freeze material harm at 0.5 SD of H before fitting. Supportive requires a positive exact-exposure Delta above that threshold with uncertainty supporting Delta > 0.5 SD, stable admissible donor/mapping/round sensitivities, coherent primary components, no matching selective pattern in LPS or FLS-only controls, and a gated 8316 secondary response that is directionally compatible without asserting a shared effect. It supports balanced agonism/genetic-loss-of-function, protein/phospho-MerTK, viability, efferocytosis and fibroblast invasion or matrix-degradation follow-up.

Adverse means Delta is nonpositive, Mneg harm is at least as large, generic controls reproduce the apparent selectivity, or a validly gated 8316 perturbation response is discordant. This weakens the context-selective prioritization rationale and favors generic inflammation, composition, timing or assay-specific explanations.

Inconclusive means the primary rank/overlap gate fails, an admissible mapping changes sign, uncertainty spans zero or the material threshold, one membership cluster drives the result, exact and preInhibitor tiers disagree without protocol equivalence, or 8316 annotation/protocol compatibility remains blocked. The next decision is to obtain balanced matched Mpos/Mneg FLS–macrophage donor pairs with dose, exposure time, viability, protein/phospho-MerTK, efferocytosis, secreted mediators and direct FLS functional readouts.

Harbor can verify source-local joins, feature presence, paired contrasts, rank calculations, uncertainty outputs, compatibility status and rule-consistent conclusions. It cannot establish clinical benefit, direct molecular mechanism, viability, spatial localization, therapeutic window, or independent biological validity; those require expert adjudication, orthogonal perturbation and another study.

## Scientific deliverable and evidence boundary

The actual deliverable is newly fitted 8873 `Delta`, context-specific effects and component effects with uncertainty; a primary identifiability report; LPS/FLS-only/composition controls; donor/mapping/tier sensitivity; a source-local 8316 paired-response and compatibility report (or an explicit blocked status); and a fit-or-defer record for the multivariate alternative. Required outputs are `analysis_manifest.json`, `effects.csv`, `controls.csv`, `sensitivity.csv`, `source_compatibility.json`, `method_comparison.json`, and `results.json`, with `results.json` linking every conclusion to computed rows. Readiness and the planned design are not a scientific result.

Unavailable evidence remains explicit: no clinical outcomes, dose-response, exposure-time field, viability, protein/phospho-MerTK, efferocytosis, secreted mediators, spatial localization, direct FLS invasion/matrix degradation, or independent balanced FLS validation cohort is configured. The 8316 source cannot fill those gaps and is not an external validation of 8873.

## Key references

[K1] establishes the remission-associated MerTK-positive macrophage and fibroblast-repair prior; it does not establish the interaction tested here.
[K2] supplies the strongest inflammatory macrophage–fibroblast rival; it does not establish MerTK specificity.
[K3] bounds the FLS harm endpoint as heterogeneous and niche-linked; it does not validate this panel or assay transfer.

Attached branch files preserve exactly these three inspected works and bounded source excerpts: `key-references.json`, `evidence-K1-alivernini-2020.txt`, `evidence-K2-kuo-2019.txt`, and `evidence-K3-korsunsky-2022.txt`.

# Independent, source-specific triangulation of context-selective MerTK harm

Status: substantive successor of candidate-e2c88fac21f4420df13909b9. Planned Harbor experiment only; no screening or scientific result has been executed.

## Opening and hypothesis

The inspected evidence supports a broad starting claim: MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states are associated with remission/repair and MerTK perturbation has been associated with increased FLS inflammatory transcripts [K1]. It does not establish that inhibitor harm is larger in MerTK/CD206-positive than MerTK/CD206-negative context, or that the observation transfers to an independently designed paired perturbation assay.

Primary hypothesis: in E-MTAB-8873 type-B synovial-cell cocultures, exact macrophage MerTK-inhibitor exposure produces a larger FLS harm response in MerTK/CD206pos than MerTK/CD206neg coculture after accounting for contributing FLS and macrophage memberships. Secondary triangulation hypothesis: within E-MTAB-8316, paired UNC106238 response in synovial monocyte preparations is directionally compatible with the primary perturbation response when summarized with a frozen verified gene map and nested donor-aware units. The secondary is not a claim that E-MTAB-8316 contains Mpos/Mneg contexts or FLS coculture harm.

The strongest rivals are generic inflammatory/stress signaling or composition, and timing/protocol mismatch. They predict similar perturbation direction in LPS controls, FLS-only samples, or all macrophage contexts; and they predict that any E-MTAB-8316 disagreement could reflect its different compound, monocyte label and absent time field. [K2] makes the macrophage-state rival consequential; [K3] shows why heterogeneous, niche-linked FLS programs must not be reduced to one transcript. The advance over [K1] is a prespecified identifiability gate plus a directional source-specific transfer check, not pooled external validation.

## Data bindings and population

All source files are read-only. Prepared matrices and designs are analysis tables; archive members are provenance, not extra observations.

Primary E-MTAB-8873:

- Matrix: [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 d218d3c46b652d533673c9ffc7876585bc51a39371f036e92d3ce568f28a4c0f. Verified header has 33 sample columns and 445 feature rows. Measured rows include MERTK|NM_006343.2|Reference_end, MRC1|NM_002438.3|Reference_end, TREM2|NM_018965.3|Reference_end, SPP1|NM_000582.2|Reference_end, IL1B|NM_000576.2|Reference_end, IL6|NM_000600.4|Reference_end, MMP1|NM_002421.3|Reference_end, MMP3|NM_002422.4|Reference_end, MMP12|NM_002426.5|Reference_end, MMP13|NM_002427.3|Reference_end and MMP14|NM_004995.3|Reference_end.
- Design: [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.design.json, SHA-256 fd2ae05bd0e31a8ba72454b97e22a48f5e53c179370e5f4b5343f5382b217ae4. Fields are sample_id, donor_id, donor_status, age, sex, tissue, cell_type, condition, treatment, source_metadata and cells. Join only design.sample_id to counts header. Comma-separated donor memberships are dependence annotations, not independent donors.
- Registry: [private-path]/assay-registry.json, SHA-256 e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab1bd1a31c77b7f70f. It records 33 samples, 445 measured features, no verified single donors and disables ordinary donor t-tests.
- Provenance: E-MTAB-8873/E-MTAB-8873.sdrf.txt and registered R1, R2 and R5 R*_SA*_..._RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz members listed in configured metadata.

Eligible rows have tissue=synovial membrane, cell_type=type B synovial cell and documented coculture. Context is the design label co-cultured with MerTK/CD206pos macrophages versus co-cultured with MerTK/CD206neg macrophages. Exact primary treatment is macrophages pre-treated with MerTK inhibitor. Exact treated rows are R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_Inhibitor, R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor and R1_SA256A_FLS_SA260R_Mpos_Inhibitor. The last has no unambiguous untreated counterpart. R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos_preInhibitor and R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos_preInhibitor remain a separate tier and are not silently pooled. R1_SA256A_FLS_SA260R_Mpos has conflicting donor metadata and is sensitivity-only. Mixed-composition, not-cocultured and six FLS-only rows are controls or descriptive strata. There is no clinical time field.

Secondary E-MTAB-8316 is source-specific and is never joined to E-MTAB-8873:

- Matrix: [private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 9ceb4b7cf3d52d7f6e3800c827d491b174b646826fae9c6d1433c5d64b219645. It has 12 sample columns and 58,302 Ensembl-indexed feature rows; header IDs are MK11, MK12, MK15, MK16, MK19, MK20, MK23, MK24, MK3, MK4, MK7 and MK8.
- Design: [private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.design.json, SHA-256 ca011580853bbea30b4f68f21bb5b017721c3e47bfefee6e9083b44da04c4c81. Fields are sample_id, donor_id, other_donor_id, donor_status, age, sex, tissue, cell_type, condition, treatment, source_metadata and unit_definition. Labels are verified none versus UNC106238; no time field and no Mpos/Mneg label. Unit definition is FLS donor cluster; monocyte donors nested and balanced across compound conditions.
- Registry: same assay-registry path; it records 12 samples, 58,302 features, independent donors not assumed, verified single donors SA049, SA051, SA104 and SA114, four FLS donor clusters and six nested monocyte donors.
- Provenance: E-MTAB-8316/MK_readcountMatrix.txt.gz and E-MTAB-8316/E-MTAB-8316.sdrf.txt, source hashes 510b69e449ed424adfbf225b8eeaf9faff1f8a973c76951612caf7ae69103228 and 3e304fc612102181c9106532d42b010554f342b8529f6542c04169e50093ce74.

The six verified within-source pairs are MK11/MK12 (SA114, other_donor_id 1533), MK15/MK16 (SA114, 1534), MK19/MK20 (SA051, 1601), MK23/MK24 (SA104, 1602), MK3/MK4 (SA049, 1462), and MK7/MK8 (SA049, 1463), first none and second UNC106238. No identifier, donor, specimen or row may be joined across assays. E-MTAB-8316 cells are monocyte; FLS donor cluster is a nesting unit, not evidence that its readout is FLS harm.

The feature-header inspection found no rows named MERTK, MRC1, TREM2, SPP1, IL1B, IL6, MMP1, MMP3, MMP12, MMP13, MMP14, TNF or CXCL8 in E-MTAB-8316. It is Ensembl-only. A target-module claim is gated on a named frozen Ensembl-to-transcript map and protocol reconciliation. If absent, secondary status is mapping_blocked, not zero.

## Estimands, baseline and identifiability

Normalize each prepared matrix independently to log2(CPM + pseudocount), preserve identifiers and do not impute absent genes. Emit a manifest with source, sample ID, treatment tier, context, round, FLS membership, macrophage membership, nested donor unit, mapping status and exclusions.

Primary harm score H is the mean of feature-standardized IL6, MMP1, MMP3 and MMP14, standardized using eligible untreated coculture references only. Secondary outcomes are IL1B, MMP12 and MMP13 plus each component. MERTK, MRC1, TREM2 and SPP1 are a descriptive context panel, not proof of target engagement.

Primary estimand:
Delta = [E(H | exact inhibitor, Mpos) - E(H | untreated, Mpos)] - [E(H | exact inhibitor, Mneg) - E(H | untreated, Mneg)].

First report the rank/overlap gate: exposure-by-context cells, matched counterpart availability, FLS/macrophage membership incidence overlap, and whether Delta is estimable without the ambiguous untreated row or preInhibitor tier. Only the R1 SA256A/SA259A Mneg and Mpos pairs provide complete same-membership exact comparisons; one Mneg treated cluster and conflicting Mpos metadata mean a population-level interaction may be non-identifiable. Failure returns inconclusive, not zero.

Transparent baseline: construct within matched same-membership H differences, then fit a small fixed-effects model with context, exact exposure and interaction, adding assay round only when rank permits. Represent every FLS and macrophage donor as a membership incidence matrix. Use crossed random effects or penalized membership effects only after documenting rank. Report effects, intervals, component effects, donor-membership bootstrap, leave-one-round-out, leave-one-membership-out and admissible mapping sensitivities. Donor t-tests, cell counts as replication, random row splits, confounded age/sex adjustment and pooling exact/preInhibitor are prohibited.

Secondary estimand is not pooled with Delta. Conditional on the annotation gate, compute within-source log-expression differences for the six none/UNC106238 pairs, average repeated context measurements within each verified donor/condition as the registry directs, retain four FLS-cluster and six nested-monocyte strata, and fit a paired donor-aware response summary with no twelve-independent-donor claim. Compare direction and module coherence only. Without the map, output secondary_mapping_blocked.json with the missing dependency and stop that branch.

## Same-input alternative and compute

The substantive alternative uses the same E-MTAB-8873 matrix, manifest, rows and outcomes: a cross-classified multivariate partial-pooling model with feature-specific intercepts, exposure, context, exposure-by-context, round and crossed FLS/macrophage membership effects. A shared latent FLS-harm factor loads IL6/MMP1/MMP3/MMP14; MERTK/MRC1/TREM2 form a descriptive context factor; SPP1 and IL1B remain an inflammatory contrast. Its target is the distribution of the same Delta, context effects, loading coherence and probability that Delta exceeds a material threshold, not predictive accuracy. Compare sign, uncertainty width, marker coherence and membership/mapping stability. The baseline loses correlated-program information; the alternative can reveal a coherent multi-marker program or appropriately widen uncertainty.

Fit only after the primary rank gate; otherwise record alternative_deferred. A conditional E-MTAB-8316 alternative, only after an Ensembl map, is a low-dimensional paired latent perturbation score within source, not a pooled meta-analysis. Held-out unit is assay round or donor-membership cluster for stability diagnostics, not external validation. Planned future cost is 4–8 CPU cores, less than 16 GiB RAM and minutes for the 33-by-11 primary target table plus a 12-sample secondary check; this is an estimate, not a measured runtime. GPU is deferred because design identifiability, not scale, limits the study. Neural prediction, ordinary t-tests, pooling the two compounds, E-MTAB-8322 scoring without its missing map and GSE95588 validation with unresolved mapping are deferred.

## Falsification and interpretation

Fix material threshold delta=0.5 SD of H before fitting. Supportive primary evidence requires positive Delta with uncertainty supporting Delta > delta (or posterior probability at least 0.90), coherent components, stable sign across mapping and membership/round holdouts, and no selective mimicry in LPS or FLS-only controls. A gated E-MTAB-8316 result is directionally concordant only if its mapped target/module response has the prespecified compatible sign across donor strata; it cannot rescue a failed primary rank gate.

Adverse evidence is nonpositive Delta, Mneg harm at least as large, generic LPS/FLS-only mimicry, or clearly discordant gated secondary direction. This weakens context-selective prioritization and favors generic inflammation, composition or timing.

Inconclusive evidence includes rank/overlap failure, missing Ensembl map, unreconciled secondary protocol/labels, uncertainty spanning zero or delta, sign changes across mappings, one cluster driving the effect, exact/preInhibitor disagreement or a non-identifiable alternative. Next test: balanced matched Mpos/Mneg perturbation across multiple FLS/macrophage donor pairs with dose, time, viability, MerTK protein/phosphorylation, efferocytosis, secreted mediators and direct FLS invasion or matrix-degradation readouts.

Harbor can check source joins, feature selection, paired units, estimand arithmetic, rank reports, mapping gates, uncertainty and conclusion compliance. It cannot establish direct mechanism, viability, spatial localization, therapeutic window, patient selection, clinical benefit or independent biological validity. Those require expert review, orthogonal agonism/genetic loss-of-function, protein/functional assays and an independent cohort. Clinical outcomes, medication response, protein/phospho-MerTK, efferocytosis, viability, dose-response and longitudinal time course are unavailable.

## Completion deliverable and references

The deliverable is newly fitted primary Delta and context-specific effects with uncertainty, rank/overlap report, exposure-tier and LPS/FLS-only controls, donor/mapping sensitivity, fitted-or-deferred alternative, and separate E-MTAB-8316 status concordant, discordant or mapping_blocked. Required outputs are effects.csv, controls.csv, sensitivity.csv, analysis_manifest.json, results.json and, when needed, secondary_mapping_blocked.json. Readiness and a planned analysis are not a result.

[K1] supports MerTK-positive resolution/repair and inhibitor-associated FLS-response evidence; this proposal adds the state-by-perturbation estimand and transferability gate. [K2] supplies the inflammatory macrophage/HBEGF rival; this proposal uses generic controls and refuses to call a generic response MerTK-selective. [K3] bounds the FLS endpoint by showing heterogeneity and niche-linked states; this proposal requires a multi-marker score and does not infer mechanism from one gene.

The exact parent key-reference receipts and three inherited work excerpts are preserved in the support package. Local files are concise UTF-8 evidence notes; no unavailable full text or supplementary methods are claimed.

# Source-local benefit–harm gate for context-selective MerTK prioritization

Status: substantive successor of `candidate-f5f1c5b4afb7ffad9717f432`; planned Harbor experiment only. No screening or scientific fitting has been executed. “Observed” below means registry, schema and source-file inspection, not biological results.

## Scientific opening, hypothesis and decision

The three inspected works establish a bounded prior, not the proposed conclusion. MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states are associated with remission biology and can induce fibroblast repair [K1]. An inflammatory macrophage state can drive fibroblast invasiveness through tissue cross-talk [K2]. Fibroblast inflammatory programs are heterogeneous and niche-linked [K3]. The unresolved decision is whether the configured data can support a next-stage target-prioritization decision that weighs a remission-associated macrophage benefit proxy against MerTK-perturbation FLS harm.

Falsifiable hypothesis:

> A state-stratified MerTK follow-up is justified only if two source-local findings jointly pass independent identifiability gates: (1) E-MTAB-8322 remission macrophages have a stable, preregistered MerTK-associated benefit proxy above the naive/resistant reference; and (2) the exact E-MTAB-8873 MerTK-inhibitor interaction remains materially harmful in the Mpos context relative to Mneg after membership-aware controls and sensitivities. If either axis fails, these data do not support a context-selective MerTK strategy.

This is a conjunctive advancement gate, not a patient-level net-benefit estimand. The sources have no shared donor, perturbation, time field, cell composition, endpoint or verified common biological unit. No `benefit - harm` arithmetic, cross-source pooling or donor-ID matching is allowed.

The clinically important decision is whether to invest in state-stratified MerTK preservation/activation, balanced loss-of-function and orthogonal functional assays, or abandon selective MerTK reasoning in favor of generic inflammation/composition explanations. Supportive results justify follow-up only; they do not establish clinical efficacy, direct target engagement, a therapeutic window or a patient-selection rule.

## Evidence, leading explanation and rivals

[K1] supports remission-associated MerTK-positive macrophages and fibroblast repair, but not the configured benefit proxy, inhibitor interaction or clinical efficacy. [K2] is the consequential rival: inflammatory macrophage–fibroblast cross-talk could explain FLS harm without MerTK selectivity. [K3] limits any four-transcript FLS harm score because fibroblast programs are niche-linked and heterogeneous.

The leading explanation is that a remission-associated MerTK program identifies a protective macrophage context whose perturbation exposes FLS harm. Plausible alternatives are:

- Disease-state selection, treatment history, cell composition, capture depth or donor biology may generate the 8322 state score without protective MerTK biology.
- Generic stress, LPS response, assay round, composition, exposure tier or FLS baseline may generate the 8873 interaction; HBEGF-like cross-talk is a substantive rival [K2].
- The targeted FLS panel may miss invasion, matrix degradation, viability and other niche-specific functions [K3].
- Concordant source-local axes would remain descriptive and non-causal; they cannot establish direct MerTK action or a shared patient-level benefit-harm effect.

## Baseline versus substantive alternative

Both methods use the same exact source-local inputs, targets, split and uncertainty criteria.

The transparent baseline computes fixed `B) and its state contrasts in 8322, and the parent’s paired score/interaction model for `Delta) in 8873 using the incidence matrix only when rank permits. It reports component effects, controls, exact versus preInhibitor tiers, leave-round-out and leave-membership-out results. Its advantage is auditable behavior under sparse designs; it loses correlated marker structure and uncertainty sharing.

The substantive alternative is a source-stratified multivariate/mechanistic model. In 8322, fit the same seven benefit transcripts with a shared latent macrophage-state factor, gene-specific loadings, state effects and donor-level residual covariance. In 8873, fit the same 11 measured target/context/harm transcripts with feature-specific exposure/context/interaction effects, crossed FLS/macrophage membership terms and a shared harm factor. It must output the same `B) contrasts and `Delta), components, controls and uncertainty—not a surrogate prediction. The alternative can reveal whether each signal is a coherent program or a one-marker artifact; it cannot establish direct mechanism. If either source gate fails, defer that multivariate fit and report why.

The fixed split is generated once from frozen IDs: five-fold donor/sample holdout stratified by state in 8322 and by admissible membership cluster/round in 8873, reused by both methods. In 8322, this is a stability diagnostic because groups are small, not external validation. Fit any learned loadings or nuisance adjustments inside training folds; evaluate held-out contrasts/rank stability. Primary uncertainty is a cluster bootstrap over 8322 donor IDs and 8873 contributing membership clusters, with bounded sign/permutation and leave-cluster-out sensitivity. Cells and matrix entries are never replicates.

CPU is selected: planned future solver use is 4–8 cores, <16 GiB and minutes for 19 samples/33 samples and 7/11 features; this is an estimate, not measured runtime. GPU is deferred because the bottleneck is identifiability, not matrix scale. A neural predictor is not selected because predictive gain would not distinguish donor/composition selection from MerTK biology or answer the target decision.

## Falsification and interpretation

Freeze a material threshold of 0.5 SD of `B) and 0.5 SD of `H) before fitting. These are within-source thresholds and must not be subtracted.

Supportive requires the 8322 feature/state gate to pass, remission `B) contrast above its threshold with uncertainty supporting it, stable held-out/leave-donor signs and no single marker/donor driving it; the 8873 exact gate to pass, `Delta) above its threshold with uncertainty supporting it, coherent components and stable admissible sensitivities; and no Mpos-selective LPS/FLS-only mimicry. This supports orthogonal MerTK perturbation, protein/phospho-MerTK, viability, efferocytosis, secreted mediators and direct FLS invasion/matrix-degradation testing, not clinical efficacy.

Adverse means the 8322 proxy is nonpositive/unstable, the 8873 `Delta) is nonpositive or at least as large in Mneg, a control reproduces selectivity, or the multivariate model reveals a single-marker/membership artifact. This favors generic inflammation, composition, treatment history or assay-specific explanations.

Inconclusive means a feature, state, rank, overlap or holdout gate fails; uncertainty spans zero or threshold; an admissible mapping/tier changes sign; one cluster drives the result; or state selection cannot be separated from protective biology. Do not interpret an imprecise null as refutation. The next study needs balanced matched Mpos/Mneg FLS–macrophage donors, dose/exposure time, viability, protein/phospho-MerTK, efferocytosis, secreted mediators, spatial localization and direct FLS functional endpoints.

Harbor can check joins, exact feature presence, state counts, rank, split reproducibility, uncertainty, controls and conclusion-to-output linkage. It cannot establish clinical benefit, direct mechanism, viability, spatial localization, therapeutic window or biological validity of labels without expert review and another study.

## Actual scientific deliverable and evidence limits

Completion requires newly fitted source-specific outputs:

- `benefit_effects.csv`: 8322 score contrasts, components, donor counts and uncertainty;
- `harm_effects.csv`: 8873 `Delta), components and membership-aware uncertainty;
- `controls.csv`, `holdout_sensitivity.csv`, `source_compatibility.json`, `method_comparison.json` and `results.json`, with every conclusion linked to computed rows and a supportive/adverse/inconclusive rule.

The benefit axis is only a remission-associated macrophage expression proxy. 8322 lacks FLS, perturbation, dose, time, protein, spatial and functional repair measures. 8873 lacks clinical outcomes, dose-response, exposure time, viability, protein/phospho-MerTK, efferocytosis, secreted mediators, spatial localization, direct FLS invasion/matrix degradation and an independent balanced validation cohort. The three works are abstract-level inspected excerpts; no unavailable full text or supplementary methods is claimed. Screening remains planned.

## Alternatives and selection record

The fixed-score baseline is primary because its signs and missingness are transparent under the sparse interaction and small atlas strata. The multivariate model is retained because it can expose program coherence and uncertainty sharing that a score loses; it is not a complexity bonus and is deferred on failed gates. A neural/high-dimensional predictor is not selected because it targets prediction rather than the scientific advancement decision and risks donor/composition leakage. The inherited E-MTAB-8316 branch is deferred: its six source-local none/UNC106238 pairs are monocyte measurements with no Mpos/Mneg field and no configured feature map, so they cannot repair the missing common benefit-harm estimand.

## Key references

[K1] establishes the remission-associated MerTK-positive macrophage and repair prior; this proposal adds a bounded E-MTAB-8322 benefit proxy and keeps it separate from 8873 harm.

[K2] supplies the inflammatory macrophage–fibroblast rival; this proposal uses control and component falsification rather than treating MerTK expression as mechanism.

[K3] bounds the FLS harm endpoint as heterogeneous and niche-linked; this proposal reports components and refuses to call 8322 an FLS validation cohort.

Attached are exactly three distinct inspected works: `key-references.json`, `evidence-K1-alivernini-2020.txt`, `evidence-K2-kuo-2019.txt` and `evidence-K3-korsunsky-2022.txt`.

# A benefit-axis identifiability gate for context-selective MerTK perturbation

Status: substantive evolution of `candidate-f5f1c5b4afb7ffad9717f432`; planned Harbor experiment only. No molecular screening, model fitting, or scientific result has been executed in this episode.

## Scientific opening, supported claim, and unresolved claim

The inspected evidence supports a bounded biological prior: MerTK-positive/TREM2-high or LYVE1-positive synovial macrophage states are associated with rheumatoid-arthritis remission and can induce synovial-fibroblast repair [K1]. A distinct HBEGF-positive inflammatory macrophage state can promote fibroblast invasiveness through tissue cross-talk [K2]. Fibroblast inflammatory programs are heterogeneous and niche-linked [K3]. These observations motivate target prioritization, but they do not show that inhibiting MerTK selectively harms the resolution-like context, nor that the same context carries a measurable clinical benefit in the configured assays.

The parent made the harm estimand explicit: in E-MTAB-8873, exact MerTK-inhibitor exposure might increase an FLS inflammatory harm program more in the unambiguous MerTK/CD206-positive than in the negative coculture. Its consequential limitation is that this is harm-only. A target can have a selective harm signal without a demonstrated benefit axis, and the available remission/resistant atlas might be mistaken for an external validation if incompatible units are forced together.

The smallest scientifically meaningful evolution is therefore not to add an arbitrary net-benefit score. It is to add a prespecified benefit-axis identifiability gate:

> Exact MerTK-inhibitor exposure has a larger FLS inflammatory harm effect in the eligible Mpos than Mneg coculture, but a MerTK-specific benefit-versus-harm prioritization is supportable only if an independently fitted remission-versus-resistant macrophage state axis is reproducible under donor holdout, has a verified target annotation, and can be linked to the measured Mpos/Mneg context without cross-assay donor or unit substitution.

The executable primary hypothesis is the narrowed harm claim. The benefit clause is a falsifiable gate and a required decision condition, not an established conclusion. With the currently frozen files, the benefit gate is expected to be blocked by feature namespace and context incompatibility; that is a planned identifiability outcome, not a screening result.

Clinical importance: deciding whether to preserve or activate MerTK-like resolution states requires evidence that perturbation harm is context-selective and that the selected context is clinically relevant. A supportive harm result alone justifies orthogonal target-engagement and functional experiments; it does not justify a patient-selection rule, treatment, direct mechanism, or clinical benefit claim. A benefit gate that remains blocked prevents over-prioritizing a target on a one-sided expression endpoint.
