## Estimands and identifiability gates

Normalize each source separately to log2(CPM+1), preserving feature IDs and never imputing absent genes.

Primary harm outcome is
`H_s = mean(z(IL6), z(MMP1), z(MMP3), z(MMP14))`,
where z parameters are frozen from eligible unambiguous untreated exact-context co-culture rows. The primary estimand is
`Delta_H = [E(H | exact inhibitor,Mpos)-E(H | untreated,Mpos)] - [E(H | exact inhibitor,Mneg)-E(H | untreated,Mneg)]`.
Report each component, plus MERTK/MRC1/TREM2/SPP1 and IL1B/MMP12/MMP13 contrasts. This is a descriptive/associational perturbation interaction under a pseudobulk assay, not a clinical or causal treatment effect.

Before fitting, emit `harm_gate.json` with: row counts for each treatment/context cell; exact counterpart availability; donor-membership incidence matrix rank; whether any cell requires mixed, preInhibitor, metadata-conflicted, or random-split rows; and model estimability. The gate fails if it relies on ambiguous mixed rows, preInhibitor rows, the conflicted SA260R untreated row, random row split, or independent-donor assumptions. With the verified design, only one same-membership R1 pair supplies all four exact cells, so a population-level interaction is not automatically identified. Rank failure or a non-estimable interaction returns inconclusive, never a zero.

The secondary atlas estimand is a source-local remission-versus-resistant state contrast, not a target effect:
`B_f = mean(log2CPM_f | verified remission donors) - mean(log2CPM_f | verified resistant donors)`,
with uncertainty clustered at donor and with the two related/unresolved SA149 rows excluded. B is a state-association axis, not a treatment benefit or transition effect. The benefit gate requires: (a) the Ensembl feature map is present and frozen; (b) target genes and a prespecified resolution module are actually measured; (c) a donor-holdout model/contrast is stable; and (d) an explicit bridge to the 8873 Mpos/Mneg context is available. Current files fail (a) and (d), so the full benefit-versus-harm estimand is not identified.

For 8316, estimate source-local paired d-vectors only after compound/protocol and feature-map checks. For GSE95588, produce a mapping/feature-quality report and descriptive contrasts only unless donor and GSM identity are independently verified. Neither source is pooled with 8873 or 8322.

## Baseline and substantive alternative

Both alternatives use the same prepared inputs, frozen row filters, normalization, biological-unit definitions, donor/cluster holdouts, and prespecified outcomes.

Simple baseline:

1. On 8873, calculate the paired four-cell `Delta_H` and component contrasts with an incidence-matrix paired-score model. Use membership-cluster bootstrap only when at least two admissible clusters exist; otherwise report the exact contrast, rank, and an honest non-population uncertainty status. Use leave-one-round and leave-one-membership sensitivity only as applicable. This baseline is transparent and auditable, but loses correlated marker structure.
2. On 8322, estimate feature-wise `B_f` and a nearest-centroid remission-versus-resistant score after a training-only variance filter, only if the annotation/measurement gate passes. Fit target is the remission versus resistant label; hold out one verified donor at a time and report held-out balanced accuracy/log loss, donor-bootstrap intervals, and sign stability. This is a feasibility state axis, not a benefit outcome.
3. On 8316, report paired within-cluster d-vectors and on GSE95588 report only gated descriptive contrasts. No donor t-tests, pooled coefficients, or cross-source donor matches.

Substantive alternative:

- On 8873, fit a cross-classified multivariate partial-pooling model to IL6/MMP1/MMP3/MMP14 with shared harm factor, feature-specific treatment/context/interaction effects, and FLS/macrophage membership effects represented by an incidence matrix. Retain target/context marker features as contrasts. The fitted target remains `Delta_H`; the alternative asks whether the harm signal is a coherent multivariate program and whether uncertainty widens when membership dependence is respected.
- On 8322, if the feature-map and measurement gates pass, fit a sparse multivariate remission-versus-resistant model (elastic-net logistic or a low-rank factor model selected before fitting) to the same Ensembl matrix. Target is the same remission/resistant label, not drug response. Use leave-one-verified-donor-out validation, donor-cluster bootstrap, held-out log loss/AUROC/balanced accuracy, feature-sign stability, and calibration. The alternative can reveal a correlated state program that nearest-centroid scoring loses; it cannot establish a MerTK mechanism without annotation and context bridge.
- On 8316, a multivariate paired response is secondary and source-local only after the same protocol/feature gates. GSE95588 is not used to rescue a result with unresolved donor mapping.

The alternative is scientifically useful because it tests whether a putative harm or remission state is a coherent biological program rather than a single marker or one row. It is deferred automatically when the relevant gate fails; complexity cannot repair missing units, labels, or features. A neural predictor is not selected: predictive gain would not identify a MerTK interaction or clinical benefit. Revisit a hierarchical cross-assay model only after a named common feature map, same endpoint, verified context, intervention identity, and compatible biological units are obtained.

Approximate future solver resources: CPU only, 4-8 cores and <16 GiB RAM for 8873; 8-16 cores and 16-64 GiB RAM for repeated sparse/low-rank fits on 27 x 33,694 atlas data; approximately minutes for the baseline and 10-60 minutes for donor-held-out alternatives, unmeasured in this episode. GPU is deferred because the limiting issue is identifiability, not matrix scale. This is a planning estimate, not an executed benchmark. The configured planning envelope is 16 CPUs, 8 GPUs, 262,144 MiB and 28,800 seconds; no GPU or screening job is required here.

## Controls, falsification, and interpretation

Controls are fixed before fitting:

- FLS-only untreated/inhibitor rows test whether an apparent signal is a direct FLS or capture effect rather than macrophage-context interaction.
- LPS-pretreated Mpos/Mneg rows test whether generic macrophage activation reproduces the context pattern.
- Mixed-cell-composition rows test composition sensitivity but never define a clean context.
- Exact versus preInhibitor and R1/R2/R5 round/tier comparisons are sensitivity analyses, not pooled replication.
- MERTK/MRC1/TREM2/SPP1 and IL1B/MMP12/MMP13 components test coherence and competing inflammatory programs.
- 8316 paired none/UNC106238 and GSE95588 drug/TNF labels are source-local perturbation or timing comparators only; they are not MerTK validation.

Freeze a material harm threshold of 0.5 SD of H before fitting. A harm-supportive result requires positive `Delta_H` above that threshold with uncertainty supporting the threshold, coherent components, stable admissible mapping/round sensitivities, and no matching selective pattern in LPS or FLS-only controls. It supports follow-up with balanced donor pairs, orthogonal MerTK protein/phospho-readouts, genetic perturbation, viability, efferocytosis, secreted mediators, and direct FLS invasion/matrix-degradation assays. It does not establish direct target engagement or clinical benefit.

A full target-prioritization-supportive result additionally requires a non-blocked benefit gate: a reproducible donor-held-out remission-versus-resistant atlas axis, verified annotation including the target, and a separately obtained context bridge. Even then, it supports a next experiment, not a net clinical benefit estimate. Under the current files, the honest expected status is harm result plus benefit-gate blocked/inconclusive.

Adverse evidence includes a nonpositive harm interaction, Mneg harm at least as large as Mpos harm, generic LPS/FLS-only mimicry, instability driven by one membership, or discordance after a valid source-local 8316 gate. This weakens the selective-harm rationale and favors generic inflammation, composition, assay, timing, or off-target explanations. A weak or non-reproducible atlas state axis is adverse to the *benefit* claim but does not refute the harm interaction.

Inconclusive evidence includes rank/overlap failure, dependence on mixed/preInhibitor/conflicted rows, uncertainty spanning zero or the material threshold, unresolved donor/GSM mapping, missing Ensembl annotation, absent Mpos/Mneg bridge, or a cross-source estimand that must be invented. Inconclusive means obtain balanced matched Mpos/Mneg donor pairs with dose, exposure time, viability, target engagement, efferocytosis, secreted mediators, and FLS functional endpoints; it is not evidence for or against a drug.

Harbor can check source-local joins, required feature presence, exact row filters, incidence rank, held-out split integrity, paired contrasts, uncertainty calculations, gate status, and rule-consistent conclusion links. It cannot establish clinical benefit, direct molecular mechanism, spatial localization, viability, therapeutic window, or independent biological validity; these require expert adjudication, missing measurements, orthogonal experiments, or another study.

## Scientific deliverable

Newly fitted or computed outputs must include:

- `analysis_manifest.json`: catalog and input hashes, source-local filters, exact included/excluded rows, and temporal boundaries.
- `harm_gate.json`: cell counts, incidence matrix/rank, estimability, and reasons for any failure.
- `effects.csv`: `Delta_H`, component effects, marker contrasts, and uncertainty status.
- `controls.csv` and `sensitivity.csv`: FLS-only, LPS, mixed-composition, tier, round, and membership checks.
- `atlas_benefit_gate.json`, `atlas_effects.csv`, and `atlas_holdout.csv`: remission/resistant state contrast, map/measurement status, donor-holdout metrics, and explicit blocked status where required.
- `source_compatibility.json`: 8316 and GSE95588 protocol, feature, donor, context, and pooling decisions.
- `method_comparison.json`: baseline versus multivariate alternative, targets, splits, uncertainty, resource timing, and fit/defer reason.
- `results.json`: every conclusion linked to computed output rows and tagged supportive, adverse, or inconclusive.

Completion is not a readiness report. It requires the primary harm estimand or a formal non-identifiability report, the benefit-axis gate result, controls/sensitivities, method comparison, and conclusions that preserve uncertainty. No result is claimed in this proposal.

## Evidence limits and alternatives not selected

Unavailable or inadequate evidence remains explicit: no clinical outcomes, remission transition data, dose-response, exposure-time field in the prepared assays, viability, protein/phospho-MerTK, efferocytosis, secreted mediators, spatial localization, direct FLS invasion/matrix-degradation readout, verified common annotation across all assays, or balanced independent Mpos/Mneg FLS-macrophage cohort.

The atlas extension is retained as a bounded feasibility branch because remission/resistant donor labels are present and can test whether a state axis is reproducible. It is not promoted to a benefit claim because the required feature map and context bridge are absent. GSE95588 is retained as an artifact/timing comparator because its feature maps and rich treatment labels may inform controls, but it is not selected as validation because donor identities are unresolved and coculture r1/r2 includes GSE57723 material. A pooled hierarchical cross-assay model is deferred because the endpoints, feature namespaces, contexts, and units differ. A neural model is deferred because no added information would distinguish mechanism from assay structure at this sample size. Evidence that would justify revisiting these decisions is a frozen Ensembl-to-gene map, verified target/intervention identity, balanced matched contexts, donor/GSM mapping, and orthogonal protein/functional data.

## Key inspected works

[K1] establishes a remission-associated MerTK-positive macrophage state and fibroblast repair association; it does not establish the interaction or benefit axis tested here.

[K2] supplies a consequential inflammatory macrophage–fibroblast rival; it does not establish MerTK specificity or equivalence of the configured assay units.

[K3] bounds the FLS harm endpoint as heterogeneous and niche-linked; it does not validate the targeted score, atlas bridge, or clinical benefit.

Exactly three distinct inspected works are attached as UTF-8 excerpts in `evidence-K1-alivernini-2020.txt`, `evidence-K2-kuo-2019.txt`, and `evidence-K3-korsunsky-2022.txt`. They are reused unchanged from the parent’s inspected evidence; no inaccessible full text or supplementary method is claimed.

# MerTK context-selectivity gate with an explicit perturbation-control residual

Status: substantive child of `candidate-decab21ae0a9e3a872d2c42f`; planned Harbor experiment only. No screening, fitting, or biological result has been executed. The audit below is observed metadata/source inspection, not an observed biological finding.

## Decision and falsifiable hypothesis

[K1] supports a remission-associated synovial macrophage/TAM-MerTK program and reports MerTK perturbation in primary macrophage–fibroblast co-culture. [K2] supplies a consequential rival: inflammatory macrophage–fibroblast cross-talk can drive fibroblast invasiveness through HBEGF/EGFR, without a MerTK-specific explanation. [K3] shows why a small fibroblast transcript panel cannot stand in for the heterogeneous stromal, matrix, spatial, viability, and invasion phenotypes.

The unresolved target-prioritization question is narrower than a benefit-minus-harm claim:

> Within E-MTAB-8873, does exact MerTK-inhibitor exposure produce a larger FLS harm response in the MerTK/CD206-positive than the MerTK/CD206-negative macrophage context, and is that context selectivity greater than the selectivity produced by the registered LPS perturbation control?

The primary estimand remains the exact source-local interaction
`Delta_I = [H(I,Mpos)-H(U,Mpos)] - [H(I,Mneg)-H(U,Mneg)]`.
The new control estimand is
`Delta_LPS = [H(L,Mpos)-H(U,Mpos)] - [H(L,Mneg)-H(U,Mneg)]`,
using the same-round R1 Mpos/Mneg LPS rows. A descriptive residual
`S = Delta_I - Delta_LPS` is reported only as “inhibitor context selectivity beyond this generic perturbation control.” It is not a target-specificity proof: LPS is not a matched non-MerTK inhibitor, the perturbations have no recorded time field, and off-target pharmacology remains possible.

The separate E-MTAB-8322 axis stays a source-local descriptive benefit proxy:
`B_remission - 0.5*(B_naive+B_resistant)`. It is not joined, subtracted, pooled, or donor-matched to E-MTAB-8873. The advancement decision is conjunctive: stable 8322 state association plus a discriminating—but still non-causal—8873 harm/control pattern. A positive result justifies an expert perturbation study, not clinical efficacy, direct mechanism, a therapeutic window, or a patient-selection rule.

## Full metadata and exact compatibility audit

The catalog is the read-only source catalog at `[private-path]/catalog.json`, SHA-256 `162ddf0148975035ee641ae75a2666bf44a7b458b050d79370ee9f550953312f`, snapshot `core-molecular-20261003`. The registry is `[private-path]/assay-registry.json`, SHA-256 `e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f`. The registry exposes four configured assay families, but this child uses only E-MTAB-8322 and E-MTAB-8873; E-MTAB-8316 and GSE95588 remain accessible and are not used to repair the missing target comparator.

### E-MTAB-8322: source-local benefit

- Analysis table: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz`, 33,694 Ensembl feature rows and 27 sample-ID columns; source SHA-256 `95bc3a964f3fbc57cde1957ec6637aaac806cedd8dfccc0526158e9068f43f36`.

The R1 SA260R untreated row has a metadata conflict and is excluded from primary inference.

No source contains a matched non-MerTK inhibitor, vehicle-controlled alternative inhibitor, genetic MerTK perturbation, protein/phospho-MerTK, viability, efferocytosis, secreted mediator, direct FLS invasion/matrix-degradation, spatial, or clinical outcome measurement.

No donor ID, sample ID, feature ID, treatment, endpoint, or time field may be joined across E-MTAB-8322 and E-MTAB-8873. Although both assays contain labels such as MERTK, their feature namespaces and biological units differ; any cross-source “benefit minus harm” arithmetic is illegal.

## Computable analysis

### Fixed score/interaction baseline

1. Freeze eligibility, features, thresholds, and partitions before fitting. In 8322, fit no cross-source quantities: compute B and its three state contrasts. In 8873, standardize IL6, MMP1, MMP3, and MMP14 using eligible untreated unambiguous co-culture rows and define H as their mean. Preserve all four components.
2. Estimate Delta_I from the exact R1 quartet. Estimate Delta_LPS from the same-round R1 LPS rows. Report S only with its formula, input rows, and the explicit label “perturbation-control residual; not target specificity.”
3. Report MERTK/MRC1/TREM2/SPP1/IL1B/MMP12/MMP13 components and the 8873 composition, LPS, FLS-only, preInhibitor, metadata-conflict, and leave-round/membership sensitivities. Do not promote a sensitivity tier into the primary estimand.
4. Use a fixed 0.5 within-source SD materiality threshold for B and H and freeze it before analysis. Report exact treatment/context cell counts, counterpart availability, feature rank, and whether each contrast is estimable. Supportive, still planned, requires all of the following: the 8322 feature/state gate passes with a materially positive remission contrast that is stable across donor holdouts and not one component/donor; the 8873 exact quartet is rank-identifiable; Delta_I is materially positive with coherent components; Delta_LPS is not comparably Mpos-selective and S is positive; composition, FLS-only, leave-round, and leave-membership checks do not reproduce the pattern; and the multivariate model does not reduce it to one transcript. This supports advancing a balanced orthogonal MerTK perturbation experiment. It does not establish target specificity, direct action, clinical benefit, or a therapeutic window.

Adverse means Delta_I is nonpositive, Mneg-selective, no larger than Delta_LPS, or reproduced by composition/FLS-only controls; the 8322 proxy is unstable/nonpositive; or the multivariate model shows a marker/membership artifact. That favors generic activation, FLS/macrophage composition, treatment-history selection, assay-round effects, or off-target explanations and argues against a context-selective MerTK strategy.

Inconclusive means an exact counterpart, feature namespace, rank, donor/membership, or control gate fails; cluster uncertainty is degenerate; the sign changes across admissible tiers; the residual is imprecise; or the only available comparator remains LPS rather than a target-negative perturbation. An imprecise null is not evidence that MerTK has no role. It cannot adjudicate whether labels represent biologically pure Mpos/Mneg cells, establish direct target engagement, or validate clinical relevance.

The smallest decisive experiment is a balanced, matched human RA FLS–macrophage co-culture with the same FLS donor paired across Mpos and Mneg macrophage contexts and the same pre-specified exposure schedule. The independent donor-pair count must be powered for the treatment-by-context interaction; cells and technical replicates cannot replace donor units. [K2] establishes HBEGF inflammatory macrophage–fibroblast cross-talk as a rival; this child uses it to interpret LPS, composition, and targeted-panel controls rather than assume MerTK specificity.

# Episode 5 evolution: specificity and negative-control hierarchy for the source-local MerTK gate

Status: planned Harbor experiment only. The bounded source audit below was executed; no biological fitting, screening, or hypothesis result was executed. “Observed” means schema/design/registry availability, not a biological result.

## Scientific change from the parent

The parent’s two-axis gate is clinically relevant but its 8873 harm axis is not yet target-specific. The strongest remaining rival is not merely generic stress: the registered Mpos/Mneg labels jointly encode MerTK and CD206, so a Mpos-versus-Mneg inhibitor interaction cannot separate MerTK from CD206 co-expression. The exact inhibitor interaction is concentrated in the R1 quartet: one Mneg untreated/inhibitor pair and one Mpos untreated/inhibitor pair. R2 and R5 contain Mpos `preInhibitor` rows, not independent exact inhibitor replications, and there is no time field.

This child changes the scientific deliverable from “an inhibitor interaction consistent with MerTK-context harm” to a staged specificity gate:

1. determine whether an exact, source-local Mpos-selective harm interaction is estimable without pooling incompatible exposure labels;
2. test whether it survives generic-activation, composition, marker-coherence, round, and contributing-donor sensitivities;
3. state explicitly that the molecular data cannot identify MerTK-specific action when MerTK and CD206 are co-defined; require an orthogonal MerTK-versus-CD206 perturbation as the smallest decision-changing follow-up.

A supportive computational result therefore advances a MerTK/CD206-context-consistent follow-up, not a MerTK-specific therapeutic claim.

## Evidence-supported claim, unresolved claim, and clinical importance

[K1] supports remission-associated synovial macrophage states containing MerTK-positive biology and repair-associated effects. [K2] supports a consequential rival in which an inflammatory macrophage state, including HBEGF-linked cross-talk, drives fibroblast invasiveness independently of MerTK. [K3] shows that stromal/fibroblast programs are heterogeneous and niche-linked. None establishes the configured benefit proxy, the configured inhibitor interaction, direct MerTK engagement in these matrices, or a clinical therapeutic window.

The strongest available data-supported premise is thus only that (a) a MerTK-associated remission state is biologically plausible, and (b) inflammatory macrophage–FLS cross-talk is a plausible harm mechanism. The unresolved claim is:

## Falsifiable hierarchy and interpretation

All thresholds are frozen before fitting at 0.5 within-source SD for `B` and `H`; they are never subtracted across assays.

1. Compatibility/estimability gate: exact feature IDs, design-to-count joins, non-mixed status, exact counterpart availability, incidence-matrix rank, and contributing-donor dependence must pass. A failure is inconclusive, not zero.
2. Exact interaction gate: estimate `Delta_exact` from the R1 quartet only, with paired/contributor-aware uncertainty. Treat it as one exact round, not independent replication.
3. Generic-activation negative control: estimate the analogous Mpos-minus-Mneg interaction for matched LPS-pretreated rows only when both Mpos and Mneg counterparts are present. The R1 LPS pair is available; R2/R5 have Mneg LPS only. If the LPS interaction is similar in sign and material magnitude to `Delta_exact`, generic activation is favored. Absence of a complete pair is inconclusive, not evidence of no generic response.
4. Composition control: use R2/R5 `1Mpos_3Mneg` and `3Mpos_1Mneg` rows only as non-inhibitor composition checks. A monotone H change tracking mixture ratio without a perturbation contrast supports composition/context confounding, not target specificity.
5. Baseline and FLS controls: FLS-only rows and `R1_SA256A_FLS_Inhibitor` are `treatment=none` and not a valid macrophage-inhibitor toxicity control. They can bound FLS baseline only. Do not relabel them as vehicle or inhibitor controls.
6. Marker-coherence control: report MERTK, MRC1, TREM2, SPP1, HBEGF, IL1B, IL6, MMP12, MMP13 and the four H components. A one-feature effect or an HBEGF/IL1B-driven pattern is adverse for target-specific interpretation. Target transcript changes in this FLS/coculture matrix are not direct target engagement.
7. Donor/round sensitivity: report leave-R1/R2/R5-out where estimable, leave-contributing-membership-cluster-out, and an analysis excluding conflicted/reused contributors. Because exact inhibition is R1-only, a failed leave-round-out stability check is expected to be inconclusive, not a refutation.

Supportive computational outcome: both source-local axes meet their own gates; `Delta_exact` exceeds its within-source threshold with coherent H components; no complete LPS control mimics it; composition and marker sensitivities do not explain it; and no single contributing cluster drives the sign. This supports a MerTK/CD206-context-consistent, not MerTK-specific, orthogonal follow-up. It does not support cross-source arithmetic, direct mechanism, efficacy, or a patient rule.

Adverse outcome: `Delta_exact` is nonpositive, Mneg is as harmful or more harmful, LPS reproduces the selectivity, mixture composition explains the H pattern, a single marker/cluster drives the result, or the multivariate analysis removes the apparent interaction. Redirect toward generic inflammation, HBEGF/IL1B cross-talk, composition, or assay context.

Inconclusive outcome: any compatibility/rank/overlap gate fails; uncertainty spans zero or the threshold; the R1-only effect cannot survive dependence sensitivity; an exposure-tier choice changes its sign; or the available labels cannot separate MerTK from CD206. This is the expected interpretation for target specificity without orthogonal perturbation.

## Smallest follow-up that can change the decision

Run a matched, donor-blocked coculture factorial experiment using the same FLS donor and macrophage donor pair:

- macrophage contexts: MERTK+/CD206+ and MERTK+/CD206−, with orthogonal surface/protein verification;
- perturbations: vehicle, a MerTK-selective perturbation, and a CD206-selective perturbation or matched CD206 blockade; include non-targeting/isotype controls;
- generic control: matched LPS activation;
- outcomes: viability plus a direct FLS invasion or matrix-degradation endpoint, with IL6/MMP1/MMP3/MMP14 and HBEGF/IL1B as molecular secondary outcomes;
- use at least two biological donor blocks and a prespecified exposure/time grid, because 8873 has neither dose nor time.

The decision-changing pattern is MerTK-perturbation harm in MERTK+/CD206+ coculture that is absent under CD206 perturbation and not reproduced by LPS, with direct functional harm and preserved viability. If MerTK and CD206 perturbations are indistinguishable, or LPS reproduces the effect, the MerTK-specific direction is abandoned. If all effects are imprecise or viability-confounded, the result is inconclusive and another matched study is required. This wet-lab dependency is essential because 8873 cannot identify it computationally.

## Baseline versus substantive alternative

Both alternatives use identical source-local inputs, outcomes, controls, split logic, and uncertainty criteria.

Baseline: a fixed molecular score computes `B` and `H` from the prespecified gene sets and estimates `Delta_exact` plus the LPS, composition, marker, round, and contributing-cluster sensitivities. It is primary because every sign, missing counterpart, and dependence assumption is auditable in this sparse design. It loses correlation sharing and a formal separation of coherent programs from one-marker effects.

Substantive alternative: a source-stratified multivariate hierarchical model fits the same seven 8322 benefit transcripts and the same 8873 12 target/context/harm transcripts, with gene-specific effects, a shared benefit/harm factor, treatment-by-context interaction, explicit composition terms, and contributing-donor random effects. The 8873 feature set is exactly MERTK, MRC1, TREM2, SPP1, HBEGF, IL1B, MMP12, MMP13, IL6, MMP1, MMP3, and MMP14. It outputs the same `B`, `H`, `Delta_exact`, every component, and the same negative controls; it is not a surrogate prediction model. It can reveal whether the apparent interaction is a coherent program or one-marker artifact and whether residual harm remains after composition terms. It cannot manufacture MerTK/CD206 identifiability.

Use a fixed split generated once from frozen sample IDs: five-fold donor holdout stratified by state in 8322, and admissible membership-cluster/round holdout in 8873. Fit loadings and nuisance parameters inside training folds. For the exact R1 contrast, report that no independent held-out inhibitor round exists; if rank or fold support fails, defer the multivariate fit rather than changing the estimand. Primary uncertainty is donor bootstrap in 8322 and contributing-membership-cluster bootstrap plus sign/permutation sensitivity in 8873; cells and matrix entries are not replicates.

CPU is selected for the future solver envelope: 4–8 cores, under 16 GiB, minutes for the 19-sample benefit and 33-sample targeted assay. This is a planning estimate, not a measured full fit. GPU is deferred because the scientific bottleneck is target identifiability and sparse replication, not matrix scale. A neural predictor is not selected because predictive improvement would not distinguish MerTK from CD206 or generic stress.

The source audit and registry checks are complete, but screening status remains planned. It cannot adjudicate direct target engagement, cell identity, viability, invasion, matrix degradation, spatial localization, clinical benefit, or the MerTK-versus-CD206 wet-lab result.

## Substantive change

The parent’s scientific direction is retained: determine whether a remission-associated macrophage context proxy and an inhibitor-associated FLS harm contrast justify an orthogonal MerTK-versus-CD206 experiment. This child repairs two grounding problems and sharpens the decision rule.

1. The E-MTAB-8322 benefit proxy is explicitly bound to the registered Ensembl namespace. The unusual map value `MRC1 -> ENSG00000260314` is not silently replaced with an external annotation.
2. The E-MTAB-8873 panel is explicitly bound to its measured `SYMBOL|RefSeq.version|assay-end` feature strings. HBEGF and C1QC are absent from the 445 measured features and are removed from computational scores; HBEGF remains a future orthogonal measurement, not an imputed covariate.
3. The R1 exact interaction is one sparse source-local contrast, not independent replication and not a cross-source decision gate. A qualitative escalation matrix may use the two source-local statuses to decide what experiment to fund, but no benefit-minus-harm arithmetic, cross-source join, clinical utility, or target-specific conclusion is permitted.

The scientific deliverable is newly estimated source-local quantities and a predeclared escalation state: a namespace/rank report; the E-MTAB-8322 remission-state proxy and uncertainty; the E-MTAB-8873 exact R1 interaction, component effects and dependence sensitivities; and a baseline-versus-hierarchical comparison whose conclusions are linked to those outputs. Completion is not a favorable result.

## Opening, evidence-supported claim, and unresolved claim

[K1] reports remission-associated MerTK-positive/TREM2-high or MerTK-positive/LYVE1-positive synovial macrophage states, including fibroblast-repair observations. That supports biological plausibility for a resolution-associated macrophage context, not the configured seven-gene score or a MerTK therapeutic window.

[K2] reports HBEGF-positive macrophages associated with fibroblast invasiveness. This is a consequential non-MerTK inflammatory rival. It motivates generic activation and inflammatory-marker controls, but HBEGF is not measured in the configured 8873 panel.

[K3] reports heterogeneous FLS states driven by local cytokine exposures and spatial signaling. Thus a four-transcript FLS score can be a reproducible assay proxy, but it is not invasion, matrix degradation, viability, or clinical harm.

The unresolved, falsifiable claim is:

> In E-MTAB-8873, does the exact R1 MerTK-inhibitor contrast produce a materially larger FLS inflammatory transcript response in the metadata-defined Mpos than Mneg context, after source-local composition, LPS, marker, round and contributing-donor sensitivities; and, independently, does E-MTAB-8322 show a remission-associated seven-gene macrophage state proxy? If both source-local statuses are supportive, is the rational next action an orthogonal MerTK-versus-CD206 experiment rather than a target-specific conclusion?

The data cannot identify MerTK versus CD206 because Mpos/Mneg are jointly defined MerTK/CD206 labels, not orthogonal target measurements. Nor can they establish direct inhibitor engagement, dose response, time course, viability, invasion, spatial localization, or clinical benefit.

1. Namespace gate: every requested feature resolves exactly, counts/design sample IDs are bijective, and no feature is substituted by a symbol or external annotation.
2. Design gate: non-mixed primary rows, exact untreated counterparts, exposure-tier labels, rank of the R1 design, and contributor membership are recorded. Failure is inconclusive and stops inferential interpretation.
3. Benefit status: supportive only if the 8322 remission proxy is positive and material for the prespecified contrasts with donor-aware uncertainty; adverse if it is nonpositive or clearly inconsistent across the two contrasts; otherwise inconclusive. This is not evidence of clinical benefit.
4. Harm status: supportive only if `Delta_exact` exceeds the frozen within-8873 materiality threshold with coherent IL6/MMP1/MMP3/MMP14 components, no complete LPS control mimics it, no mixture/composition pattern explains it, and no single contributor cluster determines the sign. Adverse includes a nonpositive interaction, Mneg at least as harmful, LPS selectivity of similar magnitude, composition explanation, a single-marker effect, or removal by the multivariate sensitivity. Any rank/uncertainty failure is inconclusive.
5. Dependence status: use donor/contributing-membership cluster bootstrap and sign/permutation sensitivity. Cells, matrix entries and repeated sample rows are not independent replicates. Leave-round-out is reported as unavailable for the exact R1 interaction because exact inhibitor exposure occurs in R1 only; that absence is inconclusive, not refutation.

Qualitative escalation matrix:

| 8322 state proxy | 8873 R1 harm interaction | permitted next decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| supportive | supportive | Commission the smallest orthogonal MerTK-versus-CD206 factorial experiment; do not claim MerTK specificity or net benefit. |
| supportive | adverse | Do not pursue a MerTK-protective direction from these data; redirect to generic inflammation, CD206/state composition, or HBEGF biology, with HBEGF measured in the next assay. |
| adverse | supportive | No cross-source benefit conclusion is allowed; treat the apparent harm as a context signal only and require expert justification before any wet-lab escalation. |
| either status inconclusive | any | Repair/adjudicate mapping, contributor metadata, or matched exposure evidence; no target prioritization. |
| namespace/design gate fails | any | Stop the computational gate and correct the source binding; do not classify as a null. |

This table is a research triage rule, not a cross-source estimand. A supportive pair does not establish a clinical decision, direct mechanism, efficacy, or patient-selection rule.

The decision-changing wet-lab test is donor-blocked coculture with MERTK+/CD206+ and MERTK+/CD206− contexts, orthogonal surface/protein verification, vehicle, a MerTK-selective perturbation, a CD206-selective perturbation or matched blockade, non-targeting/isotype controls, matched LPS, viability, direct invasion or matrix-degradation measurement, and IL6/MMP1/MMP3/MMP14 plus HBEGF/IL1B secondary outcomes. Use at least two biological donor blocks and a prespecified time/exposure grid. MerTK-specific support requires MerTK perturbation harm in the positive context, absent or materially smaller CD206 perturbation harm, no LPS mimic, preserved viability and direct functional harm. Indistinguishable MerTK/CD206 effects, LPS reproduction, or viability confounding abandons or defers the MerTK-specific direction.

## Baseline and substantive learned alternative

Both methods use identical source-local inputs, outcomes, split logic, and uncertainty rules.

Baseline (primary): compute the fixed seven-gene 8322 score and four-gene 8873 H score, then estimate the prespecified contrasts and controls. Fit within-split z parameters only on training data. Preserve every component, missing counterpart, rank result, exposure tier, and contributor cluster. This is auditable and appropriate for a 19-primary-row 8322 state comparison and a four-sample exact R1 interaction.

Substantive alternative (secondary): fit a source-stratified, cross-classified hierarchical multivariate model using the same seven Ensembl features in 8322 and the same 12 measured 8873 features (MERTK, MRC1, TREM2, APOE, C1QA, C1QB, SPP1, IL1B, IL6, MMP1, MMP3 and MMP14). Include gene-specific effects, a shared state/harm covariance structure, the prespecified condition or treatment-by-Mpos/Mneg interaction, composition terms for mixture controls, and random effects for donor/contributor membership. It must emit the same B, H, Delta_exact, components and controls. It can reveal whether a score is a coherent program or one-marker artifact and whether residual harm remains after composition adjustment. It cannot create MerTK/CD206 identifiability or an independent R1 inhibitor replicate; if rank fails, defer rather than change the estimand.

Generate one frozen split assignment: donor-blocked, state-stratified five-fold holdout in 8322 where each fold is estimable; in 8873 use round/membership-cluster holdouts only for estimable sensitivity outcomes and explicitly mark exact R1 as having no held-out inhibitor round. Use donor bootstrap for 8322 and contributor-cluster bootstrap plus sign/permutation sensitivity for 8873. Report interval width and estimability, not only p-values.

CPU is selected: 4–8 cores, less than 16 GiB, expected minutes for these small matrices; this is an unmeasured planning estimate. GPU is deferred because the bottleneck is sparse replication, contributor dependence and target identifiability, not matrix throughput. A neural predictor is not selected: there is no independent clinical outcome to predict, and incremental prediction cannot distinguish MerTK from CD206 or generic stress. A mechanistic pathway model is deferred until protein, HBEGF, viability and functional endpoints exist; fitting it now would encode unavailable biology rather than test it.

## Planned outputs and interpretation limits

The future Harbor run must create:

- `source_compatibility.json`: exact paths, hashes, feature IDs, namespace resolution, sample/design joins, row counts, rank, counterpart availability and exposure tiers;
- `benefit_effects.csv`: B contrasts, seven components, donor counts and uncertainty;
- `harm_effects.csv`: Delta_exact, four H components, 10 measured secondary components and contributor-aware uncertainty;
- `specificity_controls.csv`: LPS, composition, FLS baseline, marker, round and contributor sensitivities, with unavailable HBEGF/C1QC explicitly listed;
- `method_comparison.json`: fixed score versus hierarchical model under identical inputs/splits;
- `decision_matrix.json`: source-local supportive/adverse/inconclusive statuses and the permitted next action;
- `results.json`: every conclusion linked to computed output rows and justified uncertainty.

Harbor can check joins, namespace resolution, rank, score/model computation, uncertainty, output linkage and whether conclusions obey the matrix. It cannot adjudicate cell identity, direct target engagement, MerTK/CD206 protein separation, viability, invasion, matrix degradation, clinical benefit, or the wet-lab decision.

## Key references

[K1] Alivernini et al., *Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis* (2020), DOI 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8; abstract-only inspection. It supports the remission-associated MerTK prior, while this proposal adds namespace-corrected source-local estimands and a specificity gate.

[K2] Kuo et al., *HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness* (2019), DOI 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587; abstract-only inspection. It supplies the inflammatory rival, while this proposal verifies that HBEGF is absent from 8873 and makes it a future orthogonal measurement.

[K3] Smith et al., *Drivers of heterogeneity in synovial fibroblasts in rheumatoid arthritis* (2023), DOI 10.1038/s41590-023-01527-9; abstract-only inspection. It bounds FLS transcript interpretation, while this proposal preserves component uncertainty and requires direct functional follow-up.

No other work is used as a key reference. The three hash-linked provider-response excerpts and `key-references.json` are attached in this branch.

# MerTK-conditioned macrophage–fibroblast communication in rheumatoid arthritis

Episode 1; evolved as a targeted repair of expert seed D3-M2. This is a planned Harbor experiment, not an executed biological result.

## Scientific question and hypothesis

Rheumatoid-arthritis (RA) synovium contains macrophage and fibroblast states associated with either destructive inflammation or remission. The strongest inspected evidence supports three separate observations: HBEGF+ macrophages can induce an EGFR-linked inflammatory/invasive fibroblast response in human RA tissue [K1]; MerTK-positive synovial macrophage subsets are associated with remission and can induce a fibroblast repair response [K2]; and MERTK+ macrophage and fibroblast states are co-enriched in clinically distinct RA synovial tissue contexts [K3]. None of those observations establishes that a MerTK-conditioned macrophage state is the directional driver of a fibroblast transcriptional response, and co-enrichment can reflect shared tissue context or composition.

Hypothesis: among human RA FLS samples cocultured with MerTK/CD206-positive macrophages, macrophage pre-treatment with the recorded MerTK inhibitor will reduce a prespecified coherent inflammatory-FLS program relative to the matched untreated coculture. The reduction should be larger and more coherent than the available MerTK/CD206-negative control, should not be reproduced simply by LPS pre-treatment, and should remain after modeling the contributing FLS/macrophage donors. This is a directional perturbation hypothesis about an in-vitro molecular state, not a claim that MerTK blockade will improve RA clinically.

The key unresolved comparison is:

- MerTK-conditioned communication: Mpos macrophage pre-treatment changes the FLS program in a reproducible direction, with coherent reversal of an inflammatory score.
- Strong rival: generic macrophage activation, donor mixture, FLS composition, batch/cell-number effects, or inhibitor off-target pharmacology explains the same pattern. Those rivals predict no Mpos-specific, donor-consistent reversal or a comparable effect in Mneg/LPS controls.

What would change practice or research is not a small predictive gain. A positive result would justify target-engagement and functional coculture studies aimed at preserving or restoring a pro-resolving macrophage–stromal circuit in difficult-to-treat or relapsing RA. An adverse result would prevent MerTK state association from being promoted to a MerTK-directed fibroblast mechanism.

## Closest inspected work and substantive advance

[K1] established a human RA macrophage–fibroblast communication axis and an EGFR-dependent fibroblast consequence, but it did not test the configured MerTK-pretreated macrophage mixtures. The present experiment adds a matched perturbation boundary and explicitly acknowledges that HBEGF and EGFR are absent from the targeted E-MTAB-8873 panel.

[K2] associated MerTK-positive macrophage subsets with remission and fibroblast repair. The present experiment asks whether a recorded perturbation of the macrophage input changes a prespecified inflammatory FLS output, rather than treating a remission association as a directional mechanism.

[K3] defined clinically meaningful co-enriched MERTK+ macrophage and fibroblast states and candidate communication structure. The present experiment is a small, donor-aware perturbational test designed to distinguish communication from shared tissue context, selection and composition. It does not reproduce K3’s clinical cohort or spatial evidence.

The advance is therefore boundary testing: state association and inferred communication become a falsifiable, bounded perturbation hypothesis, with explicit failure criteria and a direct next experiment.

## Population, temporal boundary, and exact data binding

Primary population: the FLS sample columns in the prepared E-MTAB-8873 targeted matrix. The matrix is a gzipped TSV whose first column is feature and whose remaining 33 columns are the sample_id values in E-MTAB-8873.design.json. It has 445 measured feature rows (446 lines including the header). The design identifies human type-B synovial cells from RA synovial membrane, with condition, treatment, donor_id, donor_status, age, sex, and cells.

Primary matched Mpos inhibitor comparison uses only these design-matrix pairs, because both untreated and pre-inhibitor samples are present for the same recorded contributing-donor mixture:

- R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos vs R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor; donor string SA256A, SA259A; untreated versus macrophages pre-treated with MerTK inhibitor.
- R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos vs R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos_preInhibitor; donor string SA257A, SA266A.
- R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos vs R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos_preInhibitor; donor string SA266A, SA277A.

The R1 SA256A/SA260R Mpos samples have a conflicting donor representation in the prepared design (SA256A versus SA256A | SA256A, SA260R) and are excluded from the primary matched estimate until the SDRF/protocol resolves the contributing donor. The three mixed Mpos/Mneg samples (R2_SA258R_FLS_SA267R_1Mpos_SA266A_3Mneg, R2_SA258R_FLS_SA267R_3Mpos_SA266A_1Mneg, and the R5 analogue) are secondary composition controls, not pure Mpos observations. All E-MTAB-8873 records have donor_status=requires_contributing_donor_model; the FLS cells are not independent donors. No claim will call the 33 columns 33 independent biological replicates.

The matrix’s primary prespecified FLS outcome panel is restricted to measured, uniquely identified targeted rows:

- MMP3|NM_002422.4|Reference_end
- MMP9|NM_004994.2|Reference_end
- IL6|NM_000600.4|Reference_end
- IL1B|NM_000576.2|Reference_end
- CXCL8|NM_000584.3|Reference_end
- CCL2|NM_002982.3|Reference_end
- ICAM1|NM_000201.2|Reference_end
- TNFAIP3|NM_001270508.1|Reference_end

MERTK|NM_006343.2|Reference_end, CD163|NM_004244.5|PolyA_1, MRC1|NM_002438.3|Reference_end, APOE|NM_000041.3|Reference_end, ADAM17|NM_003183.5|Reference_end, and the two COL1A1 transcript rows are retained as exploratory context/QC only. The targeted panel does not measure HBEGF, EREG, EGFR, VCAM1, FAP, PDGFRA, PDGFRB or MARCO; their absence is a measurement limitation, not a negative finding.

Exact primary source and prepared paths:

- Raw E-MTAB-8873 repository metadata and MAGE-TAB: [private-path]/repository.json, E-MTAB-8873/E-MTAB-8873.sdrf.txt; the source catalog records repository SHA-256 75b17dd073e6e7fcb3390ca0314544e13ecf9fb249824ed7c1c718ca0a1da3ad and SDRF SHA-256 4e564426bb68e05d93e997a9124d42f252a19680abfe54315676893ae479f719.

Orthogonal context, kept separate by source identity: E-MTAB-8316 has prepared matrix columns MK11, MK12, MK15, MK16, MK19, MK20, MK23, MK24, MK3, MK4, MK7, MK8, with design keys sample_id, donor_id, other_donor_id, condition, treatment, age, sex, and all four verified donor clusters (SA049, SA051, SA104, SA114). Six none/UNC106238 pairs are present, but repeated contexts occur within four donors. The source records UNC106238 at 250 micromolar in the repository factors. It is an orthogonal donor-paired compound response, not proof that UNC106238 is target-specific or that its monocyte endpoint is the same as the E-MTAB-8873 FLS endpoint.

- Raw E-MTAB-8316 files: [private-path]/repository.json, MK_readcountMatrix.txt.gz, E-MTAB-8316.idf.txt, E-MTAB-8316.sdrf.txt.
- Prepared matrix [private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 9ceb4b7cf3d52d7f6e3800c827d491b174b646826fae9c6d1433c5d64b219645; prepared design [private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.design.json, SHA-256 ca011580853bbea30b4f68f21bb5b017721c3e47bfefee6e9083b44da04c4c81.

All design JSONs expose no numeric sampling-time field or time-course table. The temporal boundary is therefore the recorded endpoint of each culture/pretreatment sample; the study labels do not establish a transition, persistence interval, or clinical follow-up. Exact exposure duration, washout, vehicle and target-engagement measurements are essential missing evidence.

For completeness, the other two configured datasets remain directly accessible and read-only but are not silently pooled into the primary estimate:

- E-MTAB-8322: raw [private-path]/E-MTAB-8322 with E-MTAB-8322.sdrf.txt and per-sample *.genes.tsv, *.barcodes.tsv, *.matrix.mtx members; prepared matrix [private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 95bc3a964f3fbc57cde1957ec6637aaac806cedd8dfccc0526158e9068f43f36, and design [private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.design.json, SHA-256 4ef38a7031542ec07551d585e9a2218f2620320018b3d56a86bde5a0b672a3da. It is macrophage-only pseudobulk/single-cell material across healthy, treatment-naive, remission, resistant and undifferentiated RA states; SA149/SA149P are flagged possible related/repeated donors and are excluded from simple independent-donor inference. It can supply a separate macrophage-state context, never a participant join to E-MTAB-8873.
- GSE95588: raw [private-path]/GSE95588; prepared coculture table [private-path]/GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 f6ec16014f3adcadc223a4082620ee32347a5a9bdf4ee7f30903d7a7d258b9b5, with design GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.design.json and unresolved donor IDs; prepared d1–d4 table [private-path]/GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 41c16047ab7e1c8ad2ace7e9b0c6f376fee00afe9bd6b6f360001ed52755eeb0, with design GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.design.json. Its duplicate/date-like gene labels require the registered feature-map JSONs before naming targets, and its donor-column mapping is unresolved; coculture r1/r2 includes earlier GSE57723 lineage and is not independent validation. These files are an exploratory context branch only, not part of the primary inferential package.

## Sampling, preprocessing, analysis, and uncertainty

The solver must first emit a binding audit: each matrix header must join one-to-one to a design sample_id; each primary pair must have exactly one untreated and one pre-inhibitor Mpos sample; all excluded/conflicting and mixed-ratio records must be listed. Source files are read-only and derived matrices/results go to the workspace.

For E-MTAB-8873, apply the documented targeted-matrix convention, preserve the full transcript identifiers, remove no features merely because they are unmeasured, and filter only samples failing the explicit header/design or numeric-value audit. Normalize within matrix using a predeclared library-size/size-factor method, log-transform for score modeling, and retain raw counts for a negative-binomial sensitivity analysis. Do not merge duplicate identifiers. Report per-sample cell count, detected-feature count, library size, and all filtering decisions.

Primary outcome is the sample-level inflammatory FLS score: the standardized mean of the eight prespecified row values after normalization, with each gene’s direction fixed before fitting. The primary pairwise effect is delta_k = score(Mpos + MerTK-inhibitor)_k - score(Mpos untreated)_k for the three usable matched mixtures. A supportive direction is negative attenuation in all or nearly all pairs, with a coherent panel-level estimate and uncertainty. Secondary contrasts compare untreated Mpos with untreated Mneg where the FLS donor contribution is recorded; the one available R1 Mneg inhibitor/no-inhibitor pair is a negative-control check, not a stable estimate. LPS-treated Mpos/Mneg records are a generic activation control and are never relabeled as MerTK perturbations.

Fit the simple baseline as a prespecified per-feature donor-aware model (negative-binomial count model or limma-voom equivalent, with size factor, experiment/run and FLS/macrophage contributing-donor terms when identifiable) plus the eight-gene score model. Do not use an ordinary donor t-test on the 33 E-MTAB-8873 columns. With only three usable matched mixtures, report paired estimates, donor/mixture bootstrap or Bayesian posterior intervals, and effect directions; do not manufacture asymptotic p-values or call the result independently replicated.

Fit the substantive alternative on the same inputs: a small hierarchical multivariate latent-factor model in which the eight-gene inflammatory score is a prespecified loading block and the remaining measured 445-feature matrix can contribute only through regularized factors, with random effects for FLS donor, macrophage donor/contributing mixture, and run. The target is coherent FLS-state reversal under inhibitor, not prediction of a clinical label. Fit the alternative only on the training donor clusters and report a leave-one-cluster-out stress test across R1/R2/R5; with three clusters this is a fragility diagnostic, not external validation. Compare the baseline and alternative on signed paired effect, uncertainty coverage by donor/mixture resampling, coherence of gene-level reversal, and sensitivity to the conflicting donor record. The latent model is scientifically useful because the baseline can hide a distributed, partially correlated state behind noisy per-gene tests; it can also reveal that apparent reversal is driven by one technical module or donor. It is deferred if the sample-level design cannot support partial pooling without unstable factors.

E-MTAB-8316 is analyzed separately as a donor-paired compound-response context: average repeated other_donor_id contexts within each of the four verified donor_id clusters before any exploratory comparison, as required by the dataset guide. Use it to ask whether the compound produces a coherent monocyte transcriptional shift consistent with the proposed macrophage-state perturbation, not to confirm FLS direction or target specificity. E-MTAB-8322 and GSE95588 may be used only for source-specific descriptive context after their own feature/lineage limitations are honored.

No GPU is needed for the planned discovery or solver: the matrices are small enough for CPU linear/multivariate models, and a 16-CPU, 32–64 GB RAM allocation should be sufficient; this estimate is reasoned from the 33×445 targeted matrix and is not a measured fit benchmark. The configured planning envelope is 16 CPUs, 8 GPUs, 262144 MiB and 28800 seconds; it is a future solver envelope, not an instruction to use GPUs. A bounded CPU fit should be under minutes, but convergence and model-library availability remain unverified. No full scientific screen was executed in this episode; only schema/header/design and source-literature inspection were performed.

## Falsification and interpretation

Supportive result: the three usable Mpos matched pairs show a negative inhibitor effect on the inflammatory score, the direction is coherent across the prespecified genes, the effect is not as large in the available Mneg control, donor-aware sensitivity does not erase it, and the multivariate alternative agrees without being driven by an unmeasured feature. This supports a MerTK-conditioned FLS communication hypothesis and justifies independent factorial coculture with target engagement and functional outcomes. It does not prove direct ligand–receptor binding, MerTK target specificity, clinical efficacy, remission causality, or a mechanism involving HBEGF/EGFR.

Adverse result: the score is unchanged or increases under Mpos inhibitor, the sign is inconsistent across matched mixtures, a comparable effect occurs in Mneg or LPS controls, the effect vanishes after donor/run adjustment, or the latent alternative localizes it to a technical/composition factor. This falsifies the proposed MerTK-specific directional interpretation for this assay and redirects work toward generic activation, donor-specific biology, or assay validity. It does not prove that MerTK is irrelevant in RA.

Inconclusive result: the three matched mixtures cannot be reconciled, the donor contribution is not identifiable, counts are too sparse, the panel is not measured reliably, or UNC106238/“MerTK inhibitor” identity and exposure cannot be verified. The correct action is to obtain protocol/target-engagement information and run a new balanced factorial coculture, not to interpret a null as biological refutation.

Computationally checkable claims are the header/design joins, measured-feature availability, normalization/model execution, paired estimates, uncertainty, sensitivity results, and whether the conclusion matches the prespecified outcome. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for direct target engagement, secreted cytokines, fibroblast invasion/matrix damage, tissue localization, treatment response, flare risk, and patient benefit. The verifier must reject both incorrect computation and unsupported claims that a QA result proves mechanism or clinical efficacy.

## Method alternatives and selection record

The simple donor-aware score/feature model was selected as the primary baseline because it is transparent, aligned to the limited matched design, and gives an interpretable falsification test. The hierarchical multivariate factor alternative is retained because it can reveal distributed state coherence and donor heterogeneity that separate gene tests lose; it is not selected as the sole method because three usable Mpos pairs and the targeted panel do not support an unconstrained latent model. A mechanistic ligand–receptor mediation model is deferred: the primary targeted matrix is FLS-focused and lacks HBEGF/EGFR, direct ligand abundance, protein secretion, target engagement and a balanced factorial design. Evidence that would justify revisiting it is a verified ligand-containing assay, independent FLS/macrophage donors, vehicle/washout details, direct MerTK engagement, and a functional FLS endpoint.

The actual scientific deliverable is newly fitted, donor-aware estimates of the Mpos inhibitor effect on the prespecified FLS score and feature panel, plus a fitted/assessed multivariate alternative and the binding/QC audit. Completion requires those outputs, uncertainty and the supportive/adverse/inconclusive classification; a readiness package alone is not a biological result.

## Demonstration and seed dispositions

The three clinical demonstrations were treated as ambition references, not topic requirements. Delphi’s learned dated-disease-history method is not pursued because these are molecular endpoint assays without longitudinal EHR histories; its lesson is to compare a substantive learned alternative against a simple baseline, which is applied here with a multivariate FLS-state model. Oncoformer is not pursued because the configured domain has no routine EHR or chest-X-ray modality; its lab-only adaptation would answer a different predictive question, not this mechanism question. ALADYNOULLI is not reproduced because genetic inputs and longitudinal patient trajectories are unavailable; a latent-factor adaptation is retained only as a compact descriptive alternative for the current perturbation question.

D3-M1 is deferred: E-MTAB-8322 is macrophage-only and E-MTAB-8873 is targeted FLS/coculture, so whole-tissue composition versus within-cell regulation cannot be identified without tissue composition or matched whole-tissue data. D3-M3 is deferred as a longitudinal persistence claim: E-MTAB-8322 has cross-sectional treatment-naive, resistant and remission groups and no transition times; it can later support a bounded state comparison, not persistence/remission transition inference. D3-M2 is developed because its MerTK-labeled pre-treatment contrasts provide the clearest bounded perturbation test, while the unresolved target-specific and functional evidence is explicitly retained.

## Key references

[K1] Kuo D et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” Sci Transl Med. 2019. DOI 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587. Inspected full-text snapshot excerpt: work/k1-hbegf-excerpt.txt.

[K2] Alivernini S et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nat Med. 2020. DOI 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Inspected full-text snapshot excerpt: work/k2-remission-excerpt.txt.

[K3] Zhang F et al. “Deconstruction of rheumatoid arthritis synovium defines inflammatory subtypes.” Nature. 2023. DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06708-y. Inspected full-text snapshot excerpt: work/k3-ra-subtypes-excerpt.txt.

# MerTK specificity repair: a donor-blocked macrophage–FLS interaction test

Episode 4 child of candidate-5282fd53c9408f02e8752f4b. This is a planned Harbor experiment. No biological fit or wet-lab experiment was executed here.

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The clinically important question is unchanged: can a MerTK-associated macrophage state condition rheumatoid-arthritis (RA) fibroblast-like synoviocyte (FLS) behavior in a way that could motivate resolution-restoring therapy for difficult-to-treat or relapsing RA? The strongest inspected evidence is not yet target-specific. [K1] reports an HBEGF+ macrophage–FLS axis with EGFR-dependent fibroblast invasiveness, but it is a different macrophage program. [K2] reports MerTKpos synovial macrophage subsets associated with remission and an in-vitro FLS repair response. [K3] shows that macrophage and fibroblast states are structured within clinically distinct synovial contexts. These observations support a plausible macrophage–FLS mechanism and its clinical importance; they do not establish that a compound-labeled MerTK perturbation changes FLS communication through MerTK.

Hypothesis: in the prepared E-MTAB-8873 endpoint matrix, the recorded inhibitor effect on a prespecified inflammatory FLS program is larger for MerTK/CD206-positive (Mpos) macrophage cocultures than for the matched MerTK/CD206-negative (Mneg) coculture. Formally, for a matched donor/run block k, let delta_g(k) = normalized FLS outcome under macrophage pretreatment with the recorded MerTK inhibitor minus the untreated outcome. The specificity observable is the interaction I_g = delta_g(Mpos) - delta_g(Mneg), with the same construction for the eight-gene inflammatory score. A MerTK-conditioned interpretation predicts negative I and coherent negative Mpos deltas; generic activation, compound-wide off-target effects, donor mixture, cell-composition differences or assay artifacts predict a comparable Mneg response, a response that tracks LPS rather than Mpos status, or loss of the effect after donor/QC adjustment.

## Analysis, baseline and substantive alternative

First produce a binding/QC audit. Require a one-to-one matrix/design join; list every excluded record; verify the three Mpos pairs and the single R1 Mneg pair; preserve the donor conflict and mixed-ratio records; report per-sample cell count, detected-feature count and library size. Do not filter an absent gene into a presumed zero.

Normalize the E-MTAB-8873 matrix with one prespecified library-size/size-factor method, log-transform for the score, and retain raw counts for a negative-binomial sensitivity analysis. The baseline estimates the eight-gene score and each gene with donor-aware paired contrasts. The primary estimand is the signed Mpos delta across the three usable Mpos blocks, summarized by paired values and donor/mixture bootstrap or a weakly informative Bayesian interval. The specificity estimand is the single R1 interaction I_R1; it is reported as a bounded block-level contrast, never as replicated Mneg inference. The LPS contrasts and mixed-ratio samples are prespecified negative/composition checks. There are too few independent blocks for an asymptotic p-value or an independent-replication claim.

The substantive alternative uses exactly the same samples and outcomes: a strongly regularized hierarchical multivariate latent-state model with the eight-gene inflammatory score as an anchored loading block and the remaining measured rows allowed to contribute only through shrinkage-controlled factors. Random effects represent FLS donor, macrophage/contributing mixture and run when identifiable. Its target is an Mpos-by-inhibitor state interaction, not a clinical label. Fit it on donor clusters and run leave-one-cluster-out stress tests across R1/R2/R5; with three usable clusters this is a fragility diagnostic, not external validation. Compare baseline and alternative on signed Mpos delta, the R1 interaction, gene-level coherence, donor/mixture resampling uncertainty, sensitivity to the donor conflict, and whether the alternative's signal is a generic activation or technical factor.

The alternative is scientifically substantive because separate per-gene tests can miss a distributed correlated FLS state and can fail to reveal that a nominal score is carried by one donor or technical module. It is not selected as the sole method because three usable Mpos blocks and one Mneg interaction block cannot support an unconstrained latent model. It is deferred if shrinkage diagnostics or leave-one-cluster-out fits are unstable. A ligand–receptor/mediation model is also deferred: HBEGF/EGFR and direct ligand/protein, secretion, target-engagement and functional data are absent from the primary panel. Evidence to revisit it is a verified ligand-containing assay, balanced independent donors, protocol exposure/washout, direct MerTK engagement and functional FLS endpoints.

Resource estimate: CPU is appropriate. The targeted matrix is only 33 x 445, and a 16-CPU, 32–64 GiB allocation should fit the baseline and small regularized alternative; this is a reasoned estimate, not a measured full fit. No GPU is required. The configured future solver envelope is up to 16 CPUs, 8 GPUs, 262144 MiB and 28800 seconds; discovery did not spend that envelope, and no full scientific fit was executed.

Actual scientific deliverable: a completed binding/QC audit; newly fitted donor-aware per-gene and score estimates for the three Mpos pairs; the R1 Mpos-versus-Mneg interaction with uncertainty appropriate to one block; prespecified LPS/mixed-ratio sensitivity outputs; a fitted and stress-tested multivariate alternative or a documented stability deferral; and a supportive/adverse/inconclusive classification tied to those computed outputs. Readiness alone is not completion.

## Interpretation and falsification

Supportive evidence requires all of the following as a pattern, not one favorable gene: (1) negative Mpos inhibitor deltas in all or nearly all usable pairs; (2) coherent negative movement of the fixed eight-gene score; (3) a negative R1 interaction because the Mneg inhibitor effect is smaller, not merely an Mpos change; (4) no comparable signal in LPS-pretreated controls or mixed-ratio composition checks; (5) persistence under donor/run/cell-count/library-size sensitivity; and (6) concordance between baseline and a stable, donor-stressed multivariate alternative. This supports a MerTK-conditioned communication hypothesis for this endpoint and justifies the next wet-lab test. It still does not prove target specificity, direct mechanism or clinical benefit.

Adverse evidence is an absent/inconsistent Mpos effect, a comparable Mneg interaction response, a pattern reproduced by LPS, loss after donor/QC adjustment, dependence on the conflicting R1 record, or a multivariate factor localized to technical/library-size or composition variation. That falsifies the proposed MerTK-specific interpretation of this assay and redirects work toward generic activation, donor-specific biology, compound pharmacology or assay validity. It does not prove MerTK is irrelevant in RA.

Inconclusive evidence includes failure of exact sample/design joins, inability to resolve contributing donors or exposure/vehicle/washout, sparse or unreliable prespecified rows, unstable alternative fits, or absence of target-engagement information. A null from the single R1 interaction is imprecise and is not biological refutation. The next action is protocol recovery and the balanced wet-lab test below, not favorable reclassification.

Computationally checkable claims are source hashes and paths, header/design joins, measured-row availability, filtering, normalized values, contrasts, uncertainty, sensitivity outputs, alternative-model stability and whether a conclusion matches the prespecified classification. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for target engagement, direct signaling, secreted mediators, invasion/matrix function, tissue localization, flare, treatment response and patient benefit. A verifier must reject a numerically supportive computation paired with an unsupported claim of MerTK selectivity or clinical efficacy.

## Concrete next wet-lab test

Run the smallest donor-blocked factorial that removes the current ambiguity: the same RA FLS and macrophage donor blocks crossed by macrophage state (Mpos versus Mneg) and macrophage pretreatment (vehicle, UNC106238/recorded inhibitor, orthogonal MerTK perturbation such as MerTK siRNA or a validated blocking antibody, and LPS generic-activation control), with FLS-only wells for baseline. Use at least four independent FLS donors and four independent macrophage donors, randomized/blinded wells and technical replicates nested within donor blocks; do not count wells as independent donors. Record compound identity, concentration, vehicle, pretreatment duration, washout and culture endpoint.

Before interpreting FLS output, verify MerTK surface abundance and pathway engagement (for example, MerTK occupancy or ligand-stimulated phosphorylation with a prespecified assay), macrophage viability and activation. On the same recorded endpoint measure FLS IL-6, CXCL8, MMP3 and MMP9, the eight-gene panel, secreted protein and a functional invasion/matrix assay. The decisive comparison is whether UNC106238 and the orthogonal MerTK perturbation produce the same Mpos-specific interaction while LPS does not and viability/vehicle controls are clean. If pharmacologic and orthogonal effects disagree despite verified engagement, classify the compound response as off-target or non-MerTK until resolved. A rescue or second chemotype is a follow-up, not required for this smallest test.

## Method and branch decisions

Primary baseline chosen: donor-aware fixed score plus per-feature paired interaction, because it is transparent, estimand-aligned and honest about one Mneg block.

Substantive alternative retained: hierarchical anchored multivariate factor model, fitted to the same 33-sample/445-feature input with donor/run shrinkage, leave-one-cluster-out stress testing and uncertainty comparison. It can reveal distributed state coherence and heterogeneity that the baseline loses, but its capacity is intentionally constrained by the sample design.

Not chosen: an unrestricted neural model, ligand–receptor mediation model or cross-dataset classifier. The reason is scientific adequacy, not a blanket complexity or GPU prohibition: the targeted panel lacks ligand/protein/engagement variables and the design cannot identify an unrestricted representation or a clinical prediction target. Evidence for revisiting these choices is the balanced orthogonal wet-lab experiment, verified target engagement, functional FLS outcomes, resolved donor/protocol metadata and independent donor replication.

The three demonstration papers in the research-ambition references were used as ambition context, not as a topic or method list. They are not reproduced here. This proposal is a targeted child repair of the valid parent and does not alter the macrophage–FLS clinical question.

[K1] Kuo D et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” Science Translational Medicine, 2019, DOI 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587. Abstract-only inspection in `k1-hbegf-excerpt.txt`.

[K2] Alivernini S et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Medicine, 2020, DOI 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Full-text HTML inspection of title, abstract and relevant passages in `k2-remission-excerpt.txt`.

[K3] Zhang F et al. “Deconstruction of rheumatoid arthritis synovium defines inflammatory subtypes.” Nature, 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06708-y. Abstract/metadata-only inspection in `k3-ra-subtypes-excerpt.txt`.

These three distinct works support, bound and challenge different parts of the hypothesis; none is treated as proof of MerTK target specificity.
