## Analysis, baseline and substantive alternative

First produce a binding/QC audit. Require a one-to-one matrix/design join; list every excluded record; verify the three Mpos pairs and the single R1 Mneg pair; preserve the donor conflict and mixed-ratio records; report per-sample cell count, detected-feature count and library size. Do not filter an absent gene into a presumed zero.

Normalize the E-MTAB-8873 matrix with one prespecified library-size/size-factor method, log-transform for the score, and retain raw counts for a negative-binomial sensitivity analysis. The baseline estimates the eight-gene score and each gene with donor-aware paired contrasts. The primary estimand is the signed Mpos delta across the three usable Mpos blocks, summarized by paired values and donor/mixture bootstrap or a weakly informative Bayesian interval. The specificity estimand is the single R1 interaction I_R1; it is reported as a bounded block-level contrast, never as replicated Mneg inference. The LPS contrasts and mixed-ratio samples are prespecified negative/composition checks. There are too few independent blocks for an asymptotic p-value or an independent-replication claim.

The substantive alternative uses exactly the same samples and outcomes: a strongly regularized hierarchical multivariate latent-state model with the eight-gene inflammatory score as an anchored loading block and the remaining measured rows allowed to contribute only through shrinkage-controlled factors. Random effects represent FLS donor, macrophage/contributing mixture and run when identifiable. Its target is an Mpos-by-inhibitor state interaction, not a clinical label. Fit it on donor clusters and run leave-one-cluster-out stress tests across R1/R2/R5; with three usable clusters this is a fragility diagnostic, not external validation. Compare baseline and alternative on signed Mpos delta, the R1 interaction, gene-level coherence, donor/mixture resampling uncertainty, sensitivity to the donor conflict, and whether the alternative's signal is a generic activation or technical factor.

The alternative is scientifically substantive because separate per-gene tests can miss a distributed correlated FLS state and can fail to reveal that a nominal score is carried by one donor or technical module. It is not selected as the sole method because three usable Mpos blocks and one Mneg interaction block cannot support an unconstrained latent model. It is deferred if shrinkage diagnostics or leave-one-cluster-out fits are unstable. A ligand–receptor/mediation model is also deferred: HBEGF/EGFR and direct ligand/protein, secretion, target-engagement and functional data are absent from the primary panel. Evidence to revisit it is a verified ligand-containing assay, balanced independent donors, protocol exposure/washout, direct MerTK engagement and functional FLS endpoints.

Resource estimate: CPU is appropriate. The targeted matrix is only 33 x 445, and a 16-CPU, 32–64 GiB allocation should fit the baseline and small regularized alternative; this is a reasoned estimate, not a measured full fit. No GPU is required. The configured future solver envelope is up to 16 CPUs, 8 GPUs, 262144 MiB and 28800 seconds; discovery did not spend that envelope, and no full scientific fit was executed.

Actual scientific deliverable: a completed binding/QC audit; newly fitted donor-aware per-gene and score estimates for the three Mpos pairs; the R1 Mpos-versus-Mneg interaction with uncertainty appropriate to one block; prespecified LPS/mixed-ratio sensitivity outputs; a fitted and stress-tested multivariate alternative or a documented stability deferral; and a supportive/adverse/inconclusive classification tied to those computed outputs. Readiness alone is not completion.

## Interpretation and falsification

Supportive evidence requires all of the following as a pattern, not one favorable gene: (1) negative Mpos inhibitor deltas in all or nearly all usable pairs; (2) coherent negative movement of the fixed eight-gene score; (3) a negative R1 interaction because the Mneg inhibitor effect is smaller, not merely an Mpos change; (4) no comparable signal in LPS-pretreated controls or mixed-ratio composition checks; (5) persistence under donor/run/cell-count/library-size sensitivity; and (6) concordance between baseline and a stable, donor-stressed multivariate alternative. This supports a MerTK-conditioned communication hypothesis for this endpoint and justifies the next wet-lab test. It still does not prove target specificity, direct mechanism or clinical benefit.

Adverse evidence is an absent/inconsistent Mpos effect, a comparable Mneg interaction response, a pattern reproduced by LPS, loss after donor/QC adjustment, dependence on the conflicting R1 record, or a multivariate factor localized to technical/library-size or composition variation. That falsifies the proposed MerTK-specific interpretation of this assay and redirects work toward generic activation, donor-specific biology, compound pharmacology or assay validity. It does not prove MerTK is irrelevant in RA.

Inconclusive evidence includes failure of exact sample/design joins, inability to resolve contributing donors or exposure/vehicle/washout, sparse or unreliable prespecified rows, unstable alternative fits, or absence of target-engagement information. A null from the single R1 interaction is imprecise and is not biological refutation. The next action is protocol recovery and the balanced wet-lab test below, not favorable reclassification.

Computationally checkable claims are source hashes and paths, header/design joins, measured-row availability, filtering, normalized values, contrasts, uncertainty, sensitivity outputs, alternative-model stability and whether a conclusion matches the prespecified classification. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for target engagement, direct signaling, secreted mediators, invasion/matrix function, tissue localization, flare, treatment response and patient benefit. A verifier must reject a numerically supportive computation paired with an unsupported claim of MerTK selectivity or clinical efficacy.

## Concrete next wet-lab test

Run the smallest donor-blocked factorial that removes the current ambiguity: the same RA FLS and macrophage donor blocks crossed by macrophage state (Mpos versus Mneg) and macrophage pretreatment (vehicle, UNC106238/recorded inhibitor, orthogonal MerTK perturbation such as MerTK siRNA or a validated blocking antibody, and LPS generic-activation control), with FLS-only wells for baseline. Use at least four independent FLS donors and four independent macrophage donors, randomized/blinded wells and technical replicates nested within donor blocks; do not count wells as independent donors. Record compound identity, concentration, vehicle, pretreatment duration, washout and culture endpoint.

Before interpreting FLS output, verify MerTK surface abundance and pathway engagement (for example, MerTK occupancy or ligand-stimulated phosphorylation with a prespecified assay), macrophage viability and activation. On the same recorded endpoint measure FLS IL-6, CXCL8, MMP3 and MMP9, the eight-gene panel, secreted protein and a functional invasion/matrix assay. The decisive comparison is whether UNC106238 and the orthogonal MerTK perturbation produce the same Mpos-specific interaction while LPS does not and viability/vehicle controls are clean. If pharmacologic and orthogonal effects disagree despite verified engagement, classify the compound response as off-target or non-MerTK until resolved. A rescue or second chemotype is a follow-up, not required for this smallest test.

## Method and branch decisions

Primary baseline chosen: donor-aware fixed score plus per-feature paired interaction, because it is transparent, estimand-aligned and honest about one Mneg block.

Substantive alternative retained: hierarchical anchored multivariate factor model, fitted to the same 33-sample/445-feature input with donor/run shrinkage, leave-one-cluster-out stress testing and uncertainty comparison. It can reveal distributed state coherence and heterogeneity that the baseline loses, but its capacity is intentionally constrained by the sample design.

Not chosen: an unrestricted neural model, ligand–receptor mediation model or cross-dataset classifier. The reason is scientific adequacy, not a blanket complexity or GPU prohibition: the targeted panel lacks ligand/protein/engagement variables and the design cannot identify an unrestricted representation or a clinical prediction target. Evidence for revisiting these choices is the balanced orthogonal wet-lab experiment, verified target engagement, functional FLS outcomes, resolved donor/protocol metadata and independent donor replication.

The three demonstration papers in the research-ambition references were used as ambition context, not as a topic or method list. They are not reproduced here. This proposal is a targeted child repair of the valid parent and does not alter the macrophage–FLS clinical question.

## Key references

[K1] Kuo D et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” Science Translational Medicine, 2019, DOI 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587. Abstract-only inspection in `k1-hbegf-excerpt.txt`.

[K2] Alivernini S et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Medicine, 2020, DOI 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Full-text HTML inspection of title, abstract and relevant passages in `k2-remission-excerpt.txt`.

[K3] Zhang F et al. “Deconstruction of rheumatoid arthritis synovium defines inflammatory subtypes.” Nature, 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06708-y. Abstract/metadata-only inspection in `k3-ra-subtypes-excerpt.txt`.

These three distinct works support, bound and challenge different parts of the hypothesis; none is treated as proof of MerTK target specificity.

# MerTK state versus composition: a source-separated macrophage–FLS test

Episode 5 child of candidate-7af45916709ab948b0d96b51. This is a planned Harbor experiment. The source audit was executed for availability and schema only; no biological fit, state score, or wet-lab experiment was executed.

## Scientific opening and falsifiable hypothesis

The important unresolved question is not whether RA contains macrophages associated with remission or fibroblasts associated with inflammation. The question is whether an apparent MerTK-conditioned FLS response is a within-macrophage-state signal, a difference in macrophage RNA contribution/cell mixture, or a generic activation/assay effect. That distinction changes whether a target-engagement experiment is warranted.

[K1] shows that a different macrophage program, HBEGF+, can promote an EGFR-dependent fibroblast-invasiveness phenotype. [K2] supports a clinically relevant MerTK-positive remission-associated macrophage state and an in-vitro fibroblast repair observation. [K3] shows that macrophage and fibroblast states can be co-structured by RA tissue context. Together they support biological plausibility and clinical importance, but none identifies a MerTK-specific causal signal in the configured targeted coculture matrix.

Hypothesis: a fixed MerTK-associated macrophage-state direction, estimated without FLS outcomes in macrophage-only E-MTAB-8322 and transferred only through genes measured in E-MTAB-8873, explains FLS inflammatory output beyond a macrophage RNA-contribution proxy. In E-MTAB-8873, the state interpretation is supported only if the fixed score remains associated with the prespecified FLS outcome after composition sensitivity, mixed-ratio checks, and donor/run dependence are accounted for, and if the parent Mpos-by-inhibitor interaction is not explained by a change in the composition proxy. If the score–outcome association is removed by the composition proxy or follows the known mixed ratios, the within-cell-state interpretation is falsified for this assay.

This is a direction-only cross-context hypothesis, not a claim that expression units, cell proportions, donor IDs, target engagement, or causal effects transfer between studies.

## Supported evidence, unresolved claim, and clinical advance

Supported by inspected evidence:

- RA macrophage programs can influence fibroblast behavior, including destructive invasiveness [K1].
- MerTK-positive synovial macrophage subsets are associated with remission biology and can induce a fibroblast repair response in a separate in-vitro context [K2].
- Macrophage and fibroblast states can co-occur in clinically distinct RA synovial contexts [K3].
- The executed source audit found a common, measured marker set in both configured sources: E-MTAB-8322 has Ensembl rows with gene symbols in its verified gene map, while E-MTAB-8873 has targeted gene/transcript rows for those markers.

Untested claim:

- The same MerTK-associated direction can be measured in macrophage-only E-MTAB-8322 and used as a fixed, rank/standardized proxy in E-MTAB-8873 to distinguish within-macrophage state from macrophage contribution/composition.

A supportive result would justify a balanced, orthogonally engaged MerTK perturbation study. An adverse result would prevent treating the current Mpos label or inhibitor contrast as evidence of a within-cell MerTK mechanism and redirect work toward mixture, generic activation, or assay reconstruction. Either result is clinically useful because it changes whether a target-specific resolution-restoring program should proceed.

This experiment still cannot establish MerTK binding or target engagement, inhibitor selectivity, direct ligand/receptor signaling, secretion, FLS invasion or matrix damage, tissue localization, flare prediction, treatment response, or patient benefit.

## Feasibility decision: what transfers and what does not

The transfer is valid only as a fixed marker direction over the measured intersection.

A prespecified score uses these exact gene symbols:

- positive MerTK-associated/resolution-side set P = {MERTK, CD163, MRC1, FOLR2, C1QA, C1QB, APOE}
- negative inflammatory/activation-side set N = {SPP1, TNF, IL1B}

The choice is frozen from the inspected MerTK remission/activation evidence and the assay’s verified available features; no E-MTAB-8873 FLS outcome is used to choose genes or weights. The score is S = mean(z_g for g in P) - mean(z_g for g in N), with equal weights. z_g is log1p library-size-normalized expression, standardized within the source and analysis unit. In E-MTAB-8322, S is computed per macrophage cell from the raw matrix and summarized per sample by the median and the prespecified upper-quartile fraction. In E-MTAB-8873, the same signed gene list is applied to the ten measured target rows after sample-level normalization, and is interpreted as a direction/rank proxy only. No absolute score calibration or expression-unit equivalence is claimed.

This is feasible because the executed audit verified all ten symbols in E-MTAB-8322 through the shared SA220.genes.tsv feature map, including ENSG00000153208 MERTK, ENSG00000177575 CD163, ENSG00000260314 MRC1, ENSG00000165457 FOLR2, ENSG00000173372 C1QA, ENSG00000173369 C1QB, ENSG00000130203 APOE, ENSG00000118785 SPP1, ENSG00000232810 TNF, and ENSG00000125538 IL1B. E-MTAB-8873 contains the corresponding exact rows MERTK|NM_006343.2|Reference_end, CD163|NM_004244.5|PolyA_1, MRC1|NM_002438.3|Reference_end, FOLR2|NM_000803.4|Reference_end, C1QA|NM_015991.2|Reference_end, C1QB|NM_000491.3|Reference_end, APOE|NM_000041.3|Reference_end, SPP1|NM_000582.2|Reference_end, TNF|NM_000594.3|Reference_end, and IL1B|NM_000576.2|Reference_end.

What does not transfer: a sample-level E-MTAB-8873 score cannot prove the number of macrophages, the fraction of Mpos cells, or a per-cell MerTK state. E-MTAB-8322 is macrophage-only and cross-sectional, not a whole-synovium composition reference. E-MTAB-8873 is a targeted, recorded FLS/coculture pseudobulk endpoint; its macrophage marker signal can be a mixture/contamination proxy, but it is not validated cell abundance. There is no cross-source donor join. The state score is therefore an assay-bounded proxy and a way to falsify an overstrong within-cell interpretation, not an independent validation cohort.

- Three usable Mpos inhibitor pairs: R1 R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos versus R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor; R2 R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos versus R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos_preInhibitor; R5 R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos versus R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos_preInhibitor.
- One matched Mneg specificity pair: R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg versus R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_Inhibitor. It is one block, not a replicated Mneg estimate.
- Mixed composition controls: R2_SA258R_FLS_SA267R_1Mpos_SA266A_3Mneg, R2_SA258R_FLS_SA267R_3Mpos_SA266A_1Mneg, and R5_SA263R_FLS_SA278R_1Mpos_SA277A_3Mneg.
- LPS controls: the recorded *_Mpos_preLPS and *_Mneg_preLPS samples in R1, R2, and R5 where present.
- Exclude R1 SA256A_FLS_SA260R_Mpos from the primary paired interaction because its untreated design record has the conflicting representation SA256A | SA256A, SA260R; retain it as a donor-conflict sensitivity record.

The assay registry is [private-path]/assay-registry.json, SHA-256 e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f3. Its E-MTAB-8322 and E-MTAB-8873 entries record 27 and 33 samples, respectively; independent donors are not assumed for either assay, and time_fields is null.

## Smallest Harbor experiment

### Stage 1: binding, score reproducibility, and QC

1. Verify one-to-one matrix/design joins, exact feature rows, shared gene-map row order, library size, detected-feature count, and cells per sample. Record every excluded record, including SA149/SA149P relatedness and the R1 donor conflict.
2. From the 27 raw E-MTAB-8322 sample matrices, normalize per cell, calculate S, and retain cell-level S, per-sample median S, upper-quartile fraction, and the number of cells. Use leave-one-donor-out summaries across the 25 verified donors; SA149/SA149P are sensitivity only. Do not use condition labels to fit weights.
3. Freeze the ten-gene set and equal weights. In E-MTAB-8873, calculate S and the separate unnormalized macrophage-marker fraction A from the measured rows. A is a composition/RNA-contribution proxy, not a validated cell fraction. Report the correlation and collinearity between S and A before any outcome model.
4. Use the terminal endpoint only. Do not impute a culture time, pretreatment duration, washout, or transition.

### Stage 2: state versus composition contrasts

For each E-MTAB-8873 sample, calculate the fixed eight-gene FLS outcome Y, S, A, library size, detected-feature count, cells, run, FLS donor component, macrophage contributing-donor string, and Mpos/Mneg/mixed-ratio/treatment labels.

Primary descriptive estimands:

- Within the three usable Mpos blocks, the inhibitor delta in Y and S, with donor/mixture-block bootstrap or a weakly informative interval; no ordinary independent-donor t-test.
- The single R1 interaction I = delta_Y(Mpos) - delta_Y(Mneg), reported as one bounded block-level contrast.
- A composition interpolation residual for each mixed-ratio sample: observed Y minus the prespecified 1:3 or 3:1 convex prediction from the closest pure Mpos/Mneg context, using the same run and FLS donor where the design permits. Report it as a stress test, not an independent validation.
- The residual state association of Y with S after adjusting for A, FLS-only context, run, library/QC variables, and the recorded contributing-donor structure. With three usable Mpos blocks and one Mneg block, this is a sensitivity description; it cannot supply a credible asymptotic p-value.

The state interpretation is weakened if S and A are nearly collinear, if mixed-ratio Y follows the linear composition prediction, if inhibitor shifts A without a stable state contrast, or if the Mpos interaction depends on one block or the donor-conflict record.

## Baseline and substantive alternative

Transparent baseline: a fixed score plus donor-aware paired contrasts. Normalize each sample once with a prespecified library-size method; use raw counts for a negative-binomial sensitivity. Estimate Y gene-by-gene and as the fixed eight-gene mean; estimate S and A without supervised fitting to Y. Summarize Mpos deltas, the single Mneg interaction, mixed-ratio interpolation residuals, score/abundance collinearity, and leave-one-run/block-out sensitivity. This baseline preserves the estimand and makes composition adjustment inspectable.

Substantive alternative: a constrained reference-projection/latent-mixture model on the same 33 x 445 E-MTAB-8873 matrix. Use E-MTAB-8322 single-cell macrophage profiles to form two frozen macrophage endmembers from the upper and lower S quartiles, and E-MTAB-8873 FLS-only rows as the measured FLS reference. On the intersection of measured features only, fit a nonnegative, library-scaled reconstruction that estimates (i) macrophage RNA contribution and (ii) a continuous macrophage-state coordinate between the two endmembers. Fit the endmembers without E-MTAB-8873 outcomes; do not use donor labels across sources. The model target is reconstruction of measured count vectors, not prediction of a clinical label.

Use leave-one-run-out stress tests across R1, R2, and R5 and leave-one-mixed-ratio-out checks. Evaluate held-out reconstruction error, recovery of the known pure-versus-mixed ratio ordering, stability of the state coordinate, agreement with the fixed-score direction, and whether the Y association persists after the model’s contribution estimate. Bootstrap only over recorded contributing-donor blocks and technical rows nested within blocks; do not treat cells, genes, or wells as independent donors. Compare the alternative with the baseline on the same Y, S, A, I, mixed-ratio residual, and uncertainty outputs.

The alternative can reveal whether a nominal high score is mostly a larger macrophage RNA component or a change in the macrophage state coordinate; the fixed score loses that separation. It is not automatically preferred. It is deferred if the measured panel cannot reconstruct the FLS-only controls, pure/mixed controls do not order as recorded, endmembers are unstable under donor leave-out, or the state and contribution coordinates are non-identifiable. A ligand/receptor or mediation model is not useful here because direct ligand/protein, secretion, target engagement, and functional FLS endpoints are absent.

Compute plan: CPU only. The primary prepared matrix is 33 x 445; raw 8322 matrices are larger but sparse and can be streamed per sample. A 16-CPU, 32–64 GiB job should fit normalization, score calculation, constrained projections, and block bootstrap within hours; this is a reasoned estimate, not a measured full fit. No GPU is required. The future solver planning envelope remains separate (up to 16 CPUs, 8 GPUs, 262144 MiB, 28800 seconds). The discovery audit used two CPU jobs totalling about two seconds of measured runtime and did not execute the scientific fit.

Actual scientific deliverable: (1) a frozen gene-to-feature map and QC/exclusion table; (2) E-MTAB-8322 cell/sample state reproducibility summaries; (3) E-MTAB-8873 S, A, Y, paired deltas, single-block interaction, mixed-ratio residuals and block-aware uncertainty; (4) the fitted reference-projection model or a documented stability deferral; and (5) a classification tied to these outputs. Readiness and source inspection alone do not complete the experiment.

## Interpretation and falsification

Supportive pattern:

- The ten-gene score is reproducible in E-MTAB-8322 across held-out verified donors, with directionally coherent cell/sample summaries rather than a single sample artifact.
- In E-MTAB-8873, the Mpos inhibitor pattern and Y association remain after A/QC sensitivity, do not simply track the mixed-ratio interpolation, and are concordant between the fixed score and a stable reference-projection model.
- The single Mneg interaction is smaller than the Mpos interaction, while LPS controls do not reproduce the same pattern.

This supports a MerTK-associated, composition-resistant hypothesis for the measured endpoint and prioritizes orthogonal engagement/functional testing. It does not prove within-cell causality, target selectivity, or clinical benefit.

Adverse pattern:

- The score is unstable across E-MTAB-8322 donor-held-out summaries; S and A are near-collinear in E-MTAB-8873; mixed-ratio responses interpolate as composition predicts; Y disappears after A adjustment; the inhibitor shifts A rather than the state coordinate; the Mneg response is comparable; or the signal is LPS-like, QC-dependent, or single-block.
- The latent alternative attributes the signal to contribution rather than state or fails to reconstruct known controls.

This falsifies the within-cell-state interpretation for this assay and supports the composition/generic/off-target rival. It does not prove MerTK is irrelevant in RA.

Inconclusive pattern:

- A required gene-map or matrix/design join fails; marker rows are sparse or absent; source scaling makes S direction non-reproducible; state and contribution cannot be separated; R1 donor metadata cannot be resolved; the mixed-ratio controls lack a comparable pure context; or all uncertainty is dominated by one block.
- The score can be calculated but there is no independent evidence that an E-MTAB-8873 macrophage marker signal represents macrophage material rather than FLS response or technical carryover.

This narrows the claim to feasibility and identifies the missing evidence. It does not justify a favorable conclusion or a biological null.

Computationally checkable claims are feature availability, exact joins, score definitions, source-separated donor handling, exclusions, normalized values, paired contrasts, composition residuals, model reconstruction, held-out stress tests, uncertainty, and whether interpretation follows the prespecified rules. Clinical and mechanistic adjudication require expert review or another study: actual macrophage cell fractions, MerTK surface abundance/occupancy/phosphorylation, compound identity/selectivity, secreted mediators, viability, FLS invasion/matrix function, tissue localization, longitudinal flare, and patient response.

## Alternatives not chosen and revisit evidence

- Parent-only Mpos inhibitor contrasts are retained as the primary perturbational context but are insufficient for state-versus-composition identification because the Mneg inhibitor contrast is a single R1 block.
- A simple unadjusted Mpos-versus-Mneg expression comparison was not selected because it confounds state with contributing RNA and FLS donor mixture.
- A supervised predictive model was deferred: 33 targeted endpoint samples, one Mneg inhibitor block, and no clinical outcome make predictive improvement scientifically secondary and high risk for leakage.
- A ligand/receptor mediation model was deferred because HBEGF, EGFR, direct ligand/protein, secretion, and target-engagement rows are not in the bound E-MTAB-8873 panel.
- Cross-source donor matching was rejected because E-MTAB-8322 donor IDs are not the same namespace as E-MTAB-8873 contributing-donor strings.
- The learned/latent alternative should be revisited only if its held-out reconstruction and mixed-ratio ordering are stable and a verified cell-composition or orthogonal macrophage reference is available. A direct MerTK engagement assay, balanced Mpos/Mneg donors, recorded exposure/washout, and functional FLS readouts would justify a new orthogonal perturbation child.

## Three key works

[K1] Kuo D et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” Science Translational Medicine (2019), DOI 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587. Abstract-only inspection; it supports a distinct macrophage–fibroblast communication precedent but not MerTK specificity.

[K2] Alivernini S et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Medicine (2020), DOI 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Full-text HTML inspection of the title, abstract, and relevant passages; it motivates the MerTK-associated state but not cross-assay calibration or compound selectivity.

[K3] Zhang F et al. “Deconstruction of rheumatoid arthritis synovium defines inflammatory subtypes.” Nature (2023), DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06708-y. Abstract/metadata-only inspection; it bounds contextual co-enrichment and the composition rival.

The attached key-references.json preserves the original receipts and hashes for the three attached UTF-8 excerpts. No unavailable full text or supplementary methods are claimed.

# MerTK state versus composition after leakage repair

Successor to candidate-c6cff8ff97890c2b43176e73. This is a planned Harbor experiment. The bounded source audit was executed for availability, exact rows and matrix/design joins only; no biological fit, score estimation, reference projection, or wet-lab experiment was executed.

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The relevant clinical uncertainty is whether a MerTK-associated macrophage state could be a resolution-restoring target that changes fibroblast-like synoviocyte (FLS) behavior, or whether the apparent signal is only more macrophage RNA, cell mixture, generic activation, donor/run structure, or compound behavior. That distinction changes whether an orthogonal target-engagement and functional coculture program is warranted.

[K1] reports a different macrophage program, HBEGF+, that can promote FLS invasiveness, establishing a macrophage–FLS interaction precedent but not MerTK specificity. [K2] reports MerTK-positive synovial macrophage subsets associated with remission and an FLS repair observation. [K3] shows that RA synovial myeloid and stromal states are heterogeneous and context-structured, including MERTK+, SPP1+ and IL1B+ populations. These works make the question clinically important and biologically plausible; they do not show that the configured targeted coculture signal is a composition-resistant MerTK mechanism.

Hypothesis: a fixed nine-marker MerTK-associated macrophage-state direction, constructed only in macrophage-only E-MTAB-8322 and transferred to E-MTAB-8873 only as a direction/rank proxy, is associated with the terminal FLS inflammatory outcome beyond a separate macrophage-RNA-contribution proxy. The hypothesis is supported only if the state association and the recorded Mpos inhibitor pattern survive composition, mixed-ratio, run, donor-structure and QC sensitivity, and agree with a stable reference projection fit that never uses FLS outcome rows.

The exact disjoint sets are frozen before any outcome comparison:

- State/proxy positives P = {MERTK, CD163, MRC1, FOLR2, C1QA, C1QB, APOE}.
- State/proxy negatives N = {SPP1, TNF}.
- State/proxy set G = P union N, nine genes.
- FLS outcome O = {MMP3, MMP9, IL6, IL1B, CXCL8, CCL2, ICAM1, TNFAIP3}.

G intersect O is empty. IL1B is outcome-only: it is not used in the score, contribution proxy, reference endmembers, QC selection, or any fitted latent coordinate. This nine-marker repair is scientifically useful because it preserves a MerTK/resolution-versus-inflammatory direction while removing the parent’s predictor/outcome coupling. It is a falsification test of a composition-resistant interpretation, not evidence of target engagement or causality.

Strongest available claim: MerTK-positive macrophage states and macrophage–FLS interactions are biologically plausible in RA, and the configured assays contain measured rows that can represent a direction associated with that literature. Untested claim: the direction is more than RNA contribution/composition in this endpoint assay. Strong rivals are (1) differing macrophage material or cell mixture, (2) generic activation/LPS-like response or technical carryover, and (3) donor/run or compound/off-target structure. The decisive observable is whether the fixed state direction adds stable information after the contribution proxy and whether mixed-ratio samples follow composition interpolation.

## Clinical importance and substantive advance

If the state-resistant pattern is present, the next consequential decision is to invest in orthogonal MerTK engagement, viability, secreted-mediator and FLS functional assays. If the pattern is explained by contribution, mixed ratios, generic activation or a single block, a target-specific resolution program should not be advanced from this assay. A negative result does not show MerTK is irrelevant in RA; it prevents an overstrong interpretation of this targeted endpoint.

The advance over [K1] is a MerTK-focused, source-separated state-versus-contribution test rather than a general macrophage–FLS interaction observation. The advance over [K2] is a leakage-free cross-assay direction test with an explicit composition rival rather than a transfer of remission biology as calibrated expression. The advance over [K3] is an endpoint-bounded comparison that treats cellular context and abundance as competing explanations rather than reading co-occurring states as mechanism. This is not an exhaustive novelty search.

## Exact data binding and source boundaries

1. Recheck one-to-one matrix/design joins, exact feature keys, gene-map row order, library size, detected-feature count and recorded cells. Save all exclusions, including SA149P/UPASA149 relatedness and the R1 donor conflict.
2. Read the E-MTAB-8322 raw matrices through the exact matrix/gene/barcode row and column ordering. Normalize per cell with one prespecified library-size method; calculate S9 per cell; summarize median S9 and upper-quartile fraction per sample. Use all 27 recorded samples for construction, but use 25 verified donor IDs for donor-aware summaries. Do not fit weights from E-MTAB-8873 or from condition labels.
3. In E-MTAB-8873, apply only the exact nine rows in G to calculate S9 and A9. Do not read O into either calculation. A9 is a macrophage-RNA-contribution proxy, not a validated cell fraction: (A9_i=1/9sum_{gin G}z_{ig}), while (S9_i=1/7sum_{gin P}z_{ig}-1/2sum_{gin N}z_{ig}). Report their correlation and collinearity before outcome modeling.
4. Construct Y only after S9, A9 and the alternative’s state/contribution coordinates are frozen. Retain endpoint-only timing and do not impute exposure or washout.

### Stage 2: baseline state-versus-composition estimands

Use (x_{ig}=log(1+10^6 c_{ig}/L_i)), with one fixed library-size normalization; standardize each feature by the prespecified source/analysis unit. Retain raw counts for a negative-binomial sensitivity, but do not use a different marker set.

Primary descriptive outputs are:

- S9, A9, Y, library size, detected-feature count, recorded cells, run, FLS donor component, contributing-donor string and design labels for every E-MTAB-8873 sample.
- Within the three usable Mpos blocks, paired inhibitor deltas in Y, S9 and A9, with uncertainty obtained by resampling recorded blocks/donor mixtures rather than cells or genes.
- The single R1 interaction (I=Delta_Y(Mpos)-Delta_Y(Mneg)), reported as one bounded block contrast and not as replicated Mneg inference.
- For each mixed-ratio sample, the observed Y minus a prespecified 1:3 or 3:1 convex prediction from the closest pure Mpos/Mneg context where the same run and FLS donor permit it. This is a composition stress test, not independent validation.
- Leave-one-run/block-out and donor-conflict sensitivity, with no asymptotic p-value claimed from three Mpos blocks and one Mneg block.

### Substantive alternative: leakage-free reference projection

Fit a constrained reference projection on the same E-MTAB-8322 raw matrices and E-MTAB-8873 prepared matrix/design, but on the nine G rows only. The eight O rows, including IL1B, are excluded from fitting, endmember construction, normalization-based feature selection and latent-coordinate estimation.

From E-MTAB-8322, construct high-S9 and low-S9 macrophage endmembers using prespecified upper and lower S9 quartiles, with leave-one-verified-donor-out versions. From E-MTAB-8873 FLS-only records, estimate a measured nine-row background reference; it is a technical/context reference, not proof of cell purity. For each E-MTAB-8873 sample, fit nonnegative, library-scaled reconstruction of its nine-row vector with two macrophage parameters: (m_i), a contribution/RNA amount, and (q_iin[0,1]), a continuous coordinate between low-S9 and high-S9 macrophage endmembers. The fitting target is reconstruction of G, not Y, treatment labels or a clinical label. No E-MTAB-8322 donor is joined to an E-MTAB-8873 contributing-donor string.

Use leave-one-run-out stress tests across R1, R2 and R5 and leave-one-mixed-ratio-out checks. Evaluate held-out nine-row reconstruction error, recovery of known pure-versus-mixed ratio ordering, stability of m and q, agreement of q with S9, and whether the post-fit association with Y remains after m. Compare baseline and alternative on the same Y, S9, A9, Mpos deltas, R1 interaction, mixed-ratio residuals and block-aware uncertainty. Y is an evaluation output only; it is never a fitting target.

The alternative can reveal whether a nominal high S9 is mostly more macrophage RNA or a changed state coordinate, information the fixed score loses. It is not automatically preferred. Defer it if FLS-only controls cannot be reconstructed, pure/mixed samples do not order as recorded, endmembers are donor-unstable, or m and q are non-identifiable. If the nine-row panel cannot separate these coordinates, that is an inconclusive result, not evidence for state.

### Compute and deliverable

The measured discovery audit job `job-02409bf89bf46b6c91f25550` completed successfully in 0.86 seconds and produced `source-audit.json); it did not fit the biology. The future experiment should use a managed CPU job, approximately 16 CPUs and 32–64 GiB, for sparse raw-matrix streaming, normalization, paired contrasts, constrained projection and block bootstrap. This is a reasoned estimate, not a measured full fit. No GPU is required: the decisive input is 33 x 445 plus nine-row references, and the scientific uncertainty is identifiability rather than neural-network capacity. The future solver envelope remains separate and is not spent by this discovery proposal.

The actual scientific deliverable is newly computed, not merely packaged:

1. A frozen feature/row map and QC/exclusion table proving S9/A9 and Y are disjoint.
2. E-MTAB-8322 cell and sample state summaries with donor-held-out sensitivity.
3. E-MTAB-8873 S9, A9, Y, paired deltas, the single bounded Mpos/Mneg interaction, mixed-ratio residuals and block-aware uncertainty.
4. A fitted and held-out-stressed reference projection, or a documented stability/identifiability deferral.
5. A conclusion classified by the rules below and linked to those outputs.

## Falsification and interpretation

Supportive pattern requires a coherent set of outputs: S9 is reproducible across E-MTAB-8322 held-out verified donors; S9 and A9 are not effectively collinear; q agrees with S9 while m does not fully explain the Y pattern; the Mpos inhibitor pattern and Y association persist after A9/m and QC sensitivity; mixed-ratio residuals do not reduce to composition interpolation; the single R1 Mneg interaction is smaller but is reported as one block; LPS controls do not reproduce the pattern; and the reference projection is stable under leave-one-run/block-out. This supports a composition-resistant MerTK-associated direction for this assay and justifies orthogonal engagement testing. It does not prove MerTK binding, selectivity, within-cell causality, secretion, FLS function or clinical benefit.

Adverse pattern is score instability across donor-held-out E-MTAB-8322 summaries, near-collinearity of S9 and A9, mixed-ratio responses following the convex composition prediction, Y disappearing after A9/m adjustment, inhibitor changing contribution rather than q, Mneg or LPS reproducing the pattern, dependence on the R1 conflict or one run, or the projection assigning the signal to m/technical structure. This falsifies the composition-resistant within-state interpretation for this assay and redirects work toward composition, generic activation, compound pharmacology or assay reconstruction. It does not prove MerTK is irrelevant in RA.

Inconclusive pattern is a required feature or join failure, unresolved contributing-donor/protocol metadata, absent comparable pure controls, unstable endmembers, non-identifiable m and q, sparse rows, or uncertainty dominated by one block. A score that can be calculated but has no validated cell-fraction interpretation remains inconclusive for mechanism. Do not convert an imprecise null into biological refutation.

Computationally checkable claims are source paths and hashes, exact row availability, matrix/design joins, disjoint feature sets, exclusions, normalization, score/proxy definitions, fitted projection, held-out reconstruction, contrast calculations, resampling, uncertainty and whether the conclusion follows the rules. Expert review or another study is required for actual macrophage fraction, MerTK surface abundance/occupancy/phosphorylation, inhibitor identity/selectivity, ligand/receptor action, secretion, viability, FLS invasion/matrix function, tissue localization, flare, treatment response and patient benefit.

## Alternatives not chosen and revisit evidence

- The parent’s ten-gene score was not retained because IL1B appears in the E-MTAB-8873 FLS outcome; using it in a predictor can manufacture association. The child changes the estimand by removing IL1B from every predictor/proxy/latent input.
- A simple unadjusted Mpos-versus-Mneg comparison was not selected because it confounds state with contributing RNA and has one Mneg block.
- The fixed nine-marker score plus paired contrasts is the baseline because it is transparent, estimand-aligned and auditable. It may lose distributed information and cannot separate contribution from state by itself.
- The constrained nine-row reference projection is retained as the substantive alternative because it can estimate contribution and a state coordinate on the same measured inputs without outcome leakage. It is deferred if held-out reconstruction, mixed-ratio ordering or identifiability fails.
- An unrestricted latent model or neural model is not selected: not because neural or GPU methods are categorically unsuitable, but because 33 endpoint samples, one Mneg block and nine verified cross-source state rows cannot identify an unrestricted representation. A larger model would add solver complexity without resolving the clinical uncertainty.
- A ligand/receptor or mediation model is deferred because direct ligand/protein, secretion, target engagement and functional FLS endpoints are absent from the bound panel.
- E-MTAB-8316 and GSE95588 are not pooled or used as validation because their feature annotations or donor mappings do not support a safe target-specific join. Revisit them only after feature-map and donor/protocol resolution.
- Continue to an orthogonal perturbation child only if the computational deliverable is supportive and a separate study supplies direct MerTK engagement, balanced independent donors, recorded exposure/washout, viability, secreted mediators and functional FLS outcomes. Revise toward composition/generic activation if adverse; defer if inconclusive.

## Essential missing clinical and mechanistic evidence

The sources do not measure direct MerTK binding or occupancy, phosphorylation/pathway engagement, inhibitor identity or selectivity, cell viability, secreted mediators, actual macrophage cell fraction, FLS invasion, matrix damage, spatial localization, longitudinal flare or patient treatment response. The targeted panel does not measure HBEGF, EREG, EGFR, VCAM1, FAP, PDGFRA, PDGFRB or MARCO; absence is not a negative result. No cross-source donor match exists. These missing elements prevent causal or clinical claims even after successful computation.

## Three key works

[K1] Kuo D et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” Science Translational Medicine (2019), DOI 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587. Abstract-only inspection; attached excerpt and receipt in `k1-hbegf-excerpt.txt` and `key-references.json`.

[K2] Alivernini S et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Medicine (2020), DOI 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Inspected HTML title, abstract and relevant passage; attached excerpt and receipt in `k2-remission-excerpt.txt` and `key-references.json`.

[K3] Zhang F et al. “Deconstruction of rheumatoid arthritis synovium defines inflammatory subtypes.” Nature (2023), DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06708-y. Inspected HTML title, introduction and relevant myeloid results passage; attached excerpt and receipt in `k3-ra-subtypes-excerpt.txt` and `key-references.json`.

No unavailable supplementary methods or inaccessible full text are claimed.

# MerTK specificity and perturbational interpretation: source-separated orthogonal context test

This is a planned Harbor experiment. The inherited source audit verified availability and joins; no biological fit, perturbation result, or wet-lab experiment was executed for this child.

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The clinically consequential uncertainty is not whether MerTK is biologically plausible in rheumatoid arthritis (RA). It is whether the recorded inhibitor response in the configured macrophage–FLS endpoint is attributable to a MerTK-conditioned macrophage state rather than to generic compound action, macrophage RNA contribution, mixed-cell composition, LPS-like activation, donor/run structure, or an unrecorded protocol artifact.

The closest inspected evidence establishes why this distinction matters but does not resolve it. HBEGF+ macrophages can promote RA FLS invasiveness through EGFR-dependent communication [K1], which shows that a macrophage–FLS axis can be functionally important but is not MerTK evidence. MerTK-positive synovial macrophage subsets have remission-associated signatures and induced an FLS repair response in vitro [K2], supporting a MerTK-conditioned hypothesis but not the selectivity of the configured inhibitor. RA synovium contains multiple co-occurring myeloid and fibroblast states, including MERTK-expressing macrophage clusters [K3], so co-expression and endpoint correlation remain vulnerable to context and composition explanations.

Hypothesis: after fixing a nine-marker state/proxy direction without using any FLS outcome row, the E-MTAB-8873 recorded inhibitor effect on the terminal FLS inflammatory program will be larger in the matched Mpos cocultures than in the Mneg coculture, will not be explained by the mixed-ratio or LPS controls, and will remain coherent after a separate macrophage-RNA contribution proxy and donor/run/QC sensitivity. A source-separated E-MTAB-8316 none-versus-UNC106238 contrast, if reproducible across its own donor clusters, may show that a compound/context shift is not unique to one E-MTAB-8873 block. It cannot by itself test MerTK specificity because its measured rows are Ensembl identifiers without a verified assay-specific feature map, its donors and protocol are source-specific, and it has no target-engagement or FLS functional readout.

The falsifiable claim is therefore deliberately narrow: a composition-resistant, Mpos-enriched terminal expression interaction is compatible with a MerTK-conditioned endpoint hypothesis. The experiment cannot establish that the recorded compound engages MerTK, is selective, changes MerTK signaling, or causes clinical benefit.

## Supported, unresolved, and unavailable claims

Supported by inspected literature and source metadata:

- Macrophage states can alter fibroblast behavior in RA, including destructive invasiveness in an HBEGF/EGFR context [K1].
- MerTK-positive synovial macrophages are associated with remission biology and an in-vitro FLS repair response [K2].
- RA synovial myeloid and stromal states are heterogeneous and context structured, including MERTK-expressing macrophage states [K3].
- The configured source files contain exact endpoint rows, matched Mpos inhibitor pairs, one matched Mneg inhibitor block, mixed-ratio controls, LPS controls, and a separate E-MTAB-8316 compound/context design, as documented in source-binding-audit.md.

Unresolved and tested:

1. Does the E-MTAB-8873 inhibitor delta differ between Mpos and Mneg in the one available Mpos/Mneg block?
2. Does a fixed nine-marker state direction add information beyond a separate contribution/composition proxy?
3. Do mixed-ratio samples behave as composition interpolation, and do LPS controls reproduce the inhibitor response?
4. Is the terminal response coherent across the three usable Mpos blocks and stable under donor/run/QC stress?
5. Is the E-MTAB-8316 recorded none-versus-UNC106238 response reproducible across its own donor clusters?

Not established by these data:

- MerTK binding, occupancy, surface abundance, phosphorylation or downstream pathway engagement.
- Compound identity, concentration, vehicle, exposure duration, washout, selectivity, inactive-analog control, or orthogonal genetic/antibody perturbation.
- Secreted mediators, viability, FLS invasion, matrix damage, spatial localization, longitudinal flare, treatment response, or patient benefit.
- A transition, persistence, or temporal mechanism. The assay registry records null `time_fields`; every estimate is restricted to the recorded terminal endpoint.

## Exact data binding and source boundaries

All source paths are read-only. Every donor namespace is source-specific; matching an SA-like string across datasets is not a join.

### E-MTAB-8873 primary endpoint

Prepared matrix: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.counts.tsv.gz`, SHA-256 `d218d3c46b652d533673c9ffc7876585bc51a39371f036e92d3ce568f28a4c0f`. It contains one `feature` column, 445 measured rows, and 33 sample columns.

Prepared design: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.design.json`, SHA-256 `fd2ae05bd0e31a8ba72454b97e22a48f5e53c179370e5f4b5343f5382b217ae4`. Join matrix headers to design `sample_id` one-to-one. Required fields are `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `other_donor_id`, `condition`, `treatment`, `cells`, `donor_status`, `source_metadata`, `age`, `sex`, `tissue`, and `cell_type`. All 33 records have `donor_status=requires_contributing_donor_model`; the recorded donor strings are mixtures/contributing-donor labels, not independent participants.

`MERTK|NM_006343.2|Reference_end`, `CD163|NM_004244.5|PolyA_1`, `MRC1|NM_002438.3|Reference_end`, `FOLR2|NM_000803.4|Reference_end`, `C1QA|NM_015991.2|Reference_end`, `C1QB|NM_000491.3|Reference_end`, `APOE|NM_000041.3|Reference_end`, `SPP1|NM_000582.2|Reference_end`, and `TNF|NM_000594.3|Reference_end`.

The audited sets are disjoint; IL1B is outcome-only.

Raw archive binding is `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.sdrf.txt` (SHA-256 `4e564426bb68e05d93e997a9124d42f252a19680abfe54315676893ae479f719`) and `repository.json` (SHA-256 `75b17dd073e6e7fcb3390ca0314544e13ecf9fb249824ed7c1c718ca0a1da3ad`). The primary matched Mpos pairs are:

### E-MTAB-8316 context/perturbation contrast

This source can test whether the recorded compound/context shift is coherent across its own donor clusters; it cannot test MerTK specificity or FLS communication.

### E-MTAB-8322 state-direction source

Prepared matrix: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz`, SHA-256 `95bc3a964f3fbc57cde1957ec6637aaac806cedd8dfccc0526158e9068f43f36`; design: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.design.json`, SHA-256 `4ef38a7031542ec07551d585e9a2218f2620320018b3d56a86bde5a0b672a3da`; raw gene map `SA220.genes.tsv`, SHA-256 `920b9e836ae82aeabe5b95932ac8a7795c6f03decff45381749e1e3cdad1f1fa`. The nine symbols MERTK, CD163, MRC1, FOLR2, C1QA, C1QB, APOE, SPP1 and TNF were verified in the map; the source is macrophage-only, cross-sectional, and never pooled by donor with E-MTAB-8873.

### GSE95588 retained but not used for target-specific validation

Prepared coculture matrix: `[private-path]/GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.counts.tsv.gz`, SHA-256 `f6ec16014f3adcadc223a4082620ee32347a5a9bdf4ee7f30903d7a7d258b9b5`; design SHA-256 `b324aeb435525132ba231663fd863faae6b676b8301d8ded18f4301a1ee45981`; required feature map `GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.txt.gz.feature-map.json`, SHA-256 `9c3af22472f6bea36ab2e66ab998ca83c944cb0e96f26a811ce5cf5739b80087`. Prepared d1-d4 matrix: `[private-path]/GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.counts.tsv.gz`, SHA-256 `41c16047ab7e1c8ad2ace7e9b0c6f376fee00afe9bd6b6f360001ed52755eeb0`; design SHA-256 `54fb86625bd5982310e14feddb17247ea2daca6ffae2e4c67c7528a1776b6bdc`; required feature map `GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.txt.gz.feature-map.json`, SHA-256 `745f4fb65a6fb643b3edc1a0c6e2d237be38c029e8ade99415061f068a49859a`. Raw members are `GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.txt.gz`, `GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.txt.gz`, `samples.soft`, and `series.soft`. Duplicate/date-like labels and unresolved donor-to-GSM mappings block target naming and independent validation; no donor cross-source join is permitted.

The complete assay registry is `[private-path]/assay-registry.json`, SHA-256 `e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f`. Its `time_fields` entry is null. The temporal boundary is the recorded terminal endpoint for each source.

## Estimand and analysis

### Primary estimand

Let z_gi be a prespecified normalized/log-transformed value for row g in E-MTAB-8873 sample i. Define P={MERTK, CD163, MRC1, FOLR2, C1QA, C1QB, APOE}, N={SPP1,TNF}, and the fixed state direction S9_i=mean(z_Pi)-mean(z_Ni). Define A9_i=mean(z_Pi,z_Ni) as a macrophage-RNA contribution/composition proxy, not a cell fraction. Define Y_i=mean(z_gi over the eight outcome rows O), with all directions fixed toward inflammatory output before any inhibitor comparison. S9, A9 and Y are terminal expression summaries, not clinical endpoints and not causal mediation variables.

For each exact matched block k, compute delta^S_k=S9_inhibitor-S9_vehicle, delta^A_k=A9_inhibitor-A9_vehicle and delta^Y_k=Y_inhibitor-Y_vehicle. The primary Mpos quantity is the three-block paired distribution of delta^Y and its relation to delta^S after A9/QC sensitivity. The specificity quantity is the R1 block interaction I_R1=delta^Y_Mpos-delta^Y_Mneg, reported as one bounded block-level contrast. The R1 donor conflict is not silently resolved. Mixed-ratio observations test whether Y and S9 follow the recorded mixture ordering; LPS observations test whether a generic activation condition reproduces the direction.

### Fixed-score baseline

Normalize the full E-MTAB-8873 matrix with one prespecified library-size/size-factor method, use log1p or log-CPM for the fixed summaries, and retain raw counts for a negative-binomial sensitivity. Fit no outcome-derived features, no adaptive marker selection and no cross-source donor matching. Estimate paired deltas for S9, A9, each outcome gene and Y, with block-aware uncertainty (three-block sign/interval summaries and donor/contributing-mixture resampling or a weakly informative hierarchical interval). Do not use an asymptotic p-value as if there were three independent participants. Report cell count, detected-feature count, library size, all exclusions and whether any required row is absent; absence is not zero.

### Scientifically substantive alternative

Fit a donor/run-aware multivariate response model to the same E-MTAB-8873 samples and the same eight outcome rows:

Y_gi = alpha_g + b_run(i) + b_contributing(i) + beta_g treatment_i + gamma_g Mpos_i + theta_g treatment_i×Mpos_i + rho_g A9_i + q_g QC_i + error_gi,

with strong shrinkage across g and only identifiable random effects. The model's target is the vector interaction theta, not a clinical label and not a MerTK engagement parameter. S9 and A9 are fixed before outcome fitting; outcome rows never enter S9/A9 construction. Fit the model on the three usable Mpos blocks plus the single Mneg block, with the donor-conflict record excluded from the primary fit and added only in sensitivity. Use leave-one-run-out (R1, R2, R5), leave-one-mixed-ratio-out and donor/contributing-mixture sensitivity. Evaluate sign/coherence of theta, predicted held-out terminal response, calibration of uncertainty under block resampling, and whether the apparent interaction is carried by one outcome gene, one run, library size, or composition.

The alternative can reveal a distributed, correlated FLS response and distinguish a coherent Mpos-by-treatment vector from a score change driven by one gene; the fixed score loses that multivariate covariance and gene-specific heterogeneity. It cannot create target engagement or identify a mechanism from expression alone. Defer it if its random effects or interaction are non-identifiable; an unstable alternative is an inconclusive result, not evidence for the hypothesis.

### E-MTAB-8316 context analysis

Within E-MTAB-8316 only, normalize the 12 samples, average repeated `other_donor_id` contexts within their own `donor_id`, and estimate the recorded none-versus-UNC106238 shift separately by the four donor clusters. Use a global multivariate distance/variance decomposition over the measured Ensembl rows and donor-aware uncertainty, not a gene-symbol or MerTK comparison. This tests donor-cluster reproducibility of a recorded compound/context shift. It does not estimate the E-MTAB-8873 FLS outcome, does not use E-MTAB-8873 donor strings, and cannot be called target-specific. If a verified feature map, compound identity, matched concentration/vehicle/exposure and direct engagement evidence become available, a prespecified cross-source gene-level comparison could be revisited.

### Alternatives not chosen

- An unadjusted Mpos-versus-Mneg comparison is rejected because state, contribution and donor mixture are confounded and only one Mneg interaction block exists.
- The fixed S9/A9 baseline is retained because it is transparent and preserves the state-versus-composition estimand.
- The multivariate interaction model is retained because it tests coherent outcome response on exactly the same samples and can expose gene/run heterogeneity; its fit is a fragility diagnostic, not independent validation.
- A ligand–receptor or mediation model is deferred because ligand/protein, secretion, direct target engagement and functional FLS endpoints are unavailable.
- A neural model is not selected, not because neural or GPU methods are categorically unsuitable, but because 33 endpoint samples, one Mneg block and no engagement measurement cannot identify a richer mechanism. A larger model would add complexity without resolving the target-specificity gap.
- E-MTAB-8316 is not pooled with E-MTAB-8873 and is not treated as an orthogonal MerTK perturbation because of its unannotated Ensembl rows, source-specific donors and missing engagement/protocol evidence.
- GSE95588 is not used as validation because its mappings/labels are unresolved.

CPU is appropriate for the 33×445 targeted matrix and 12-sample context matrix. A future managed job of approximately 16 CPUs and 32–64 GiB should fit normalization, paired contrasts, shrinkage modeling and block resampling; this is a reasoned estimate, not a measured full fit. No GPU is required. The future solver envelope is separate; discovery did not execute the scientific fit.

## Actual scientific deliverable

Completion requires newly computed, auditable outputs:

1. A source/QC table proving matrix/design joins, exact row availability, library-size and detected-feature summaries, exclusions, and all retained control records.
2. E-MTAB-8873 S9, A9, Y, gene-level deltas, three-block Mpos estimates, the single R1 Mpos/Mneg interaction, mixed-ratio and LPS sensitivity outputs, and block-aware uncertainty.
3. A fitted and stress-tested multivariate interaction model, or a documented non-identifiability deferral.
4. E-MTAB-8316 donor-cluster none-versus-UNC106238 context shifts and a global reproducibility summary, explicitly without target naming.
5. A classification whose text is linked to those outputs and does not exceed them.

Readiness or source availability is not a biological result.

## Falsification and interpretation

Supportive evidence requires a pattern: coherent direction of the three Mpos inhibitor deltas; a smaller Mneg change in the single R1 block; S9/Y association not explained by A9, library size, donor/run or mixed-ratio interpolation; no comparable LPS pattern; and agreement between the fixed baseline and a stable multivariate interaction model. Reproducibility of an E-MTAB-8316 compound shift across its four source-specific donor clusters can strengthen the narrower statement that the response is a reproducible compound/context phenomenon. It cannot upgrade the result to MerTK selectivity. Support justifies a new donor-blocked orthogonal MerTK study, not a clinical or causal conclusion.

Adverse evidence includes comparable Mneg and Mpos effects, LPS reproduction, mixed-ratio interpolation, disappearance after A9/QC adjustment, dependence on the conflicting R1 record or one run, a multivariate interaction localized to one gene/technical factor, or inconsistent E-MTAB-8316 donor-cluster shifts. This falsifies or weakens the MerTK-specific interpretation of this assay and redirects toward composition, generic activation, compound pharmacology or assay reconstruction. It does not show that MerTK is irrelevant in RA.

Inconclusive evidence includes failed joins, absent rows, unresolved contributing donors or exposure/vehicle/washout, unstable alternative fits, insufficient Mneg information, unresolvable feature annotation in E-MTAB-8316, or uncertainty dominated by one endpoint block. An imprecise null is not a refutation.

Computationally checkable claims are source hashes/paths, sample joins, row availability, predeclared scores, normalization, exclusions, contrasts, uncertainty, sensitivity, multivariate stability and whether the conclusion follows the classification rules. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for target engagement, compound selectivity, direct signaling, secreted mediators, viability, FLS invasion/matrix function, tissue localization, flare, treatment response and patient benefit.

## Exact missing experiment that would resolve specificity

Run a donor-blocked factorial with independent RA FLS and macrophage donors crossed by Mpos/Mneg and vehicle, the recorded compound, an orthogonal MerTK perturbation (validated blocking antibody or genetic knockdown), and LPS. Record compound identity, concentration, vehicle, exposure, washout and terminal time. Before interpreting FLS output, measure MerTK surface abundance and direct occupancy/binding or a validated target-engagement assay, plus MerTK pathway engagement after a prespecified stimulus. Measure viability and macrophage activation. On the same endpoint measure FLS inflammatory transcripts and proteins, secreted mediators, and a functional invasion/matrix assay. The decisive result is a replicated Mpos-specific effect shared by pharmacologic and orthogonal perturbations with verified engagement, absent in Mneg/LPS and robust to viability; disagreement indicates off-target or non-MerTK action until resolved. These data are not available in the configured sources.

## Three key works

[K1] Kuo D et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” Science Translational Medicine (2019), DOI 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587. Abstract-only inspection; excerpt and receipt in `k1-hbegf-excerpt.txt`.

[K2] Alivernini S et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Medicine (2020), DOI 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Inspected title, abstract, Fig. 5 caption and data-availability paragraph from frozen HTML; excerpt and receipt in `k2-remission-excerpt.txt`.

[K3] Zhang F et al. “Deconstruction of rheumatoid arthritis synovium defines inflammatory subtypes.” Nature (2023), DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06708-y. Inspected myeloid/fibroblast passage from frozen HTML; excerpt and receipt in `k3-ra-subtypes-excerpt.txt`.

No unavailable supplementary methods or inaccessible full text are claimed. The three attached UTF-8 excerpts are the evidence snapshots used for these mappings.

# MerTK specificity after the orthogonal-bridge audit

This is an independent, potentially deferring child of candidate-55bb151a5f564570df0a5514. It is a planned Harbor experiment. The bounded diagnostic job `job-c954bfd7492602a48269c4bb` inspected source schemas, design rows, feature-map records and matrix headers. It did not fit scores, estimate expression effects, or claim a biological result.

## Decision and scientific opening

The parent asks whether a nine-marker macrophage direction is more than RNA contribution or composition in the terminal E-MTAB-8873 assay. The remaining gap is stronger: even a stable composition-resistant direction would still be a MerTK-associated proxy, not evidence that MerTK is engaged or mediates FLS behavior.

The closest inspected work establishes why the question matters. [K1] shows that an HBEGF+ macrophage state can promote FLS invasiveness through EGFR-dependent interaction, but it is not MerTK evidence. [K2] reports MerTK-positive synovial macrophage subsets associated with remission and FLS repair and deposits the three E-MTAB assays used here. [K3] shows that MERTK+ macrophages coexist with HBEGF/IL1B and SPP1 states across context-defined synovial subtypes. These works support plausibility and a macrophage–FLS mechanism; they do not identify a MerTK-specific signal in the configured endpoint data.

The bounded audit finds:

- E-MTAB-8316 contains a genuine source-internal paired perturbation structure: four verified monocyte donors (SA114, SA051, SA104, SA049), six nested `other_donor_id` specimens and 12 samples. Each paired context has `condition/treatment=none` versus `UNC106238` at 250 µM; all records are monocytes from synovial membrane with a recorded LPS stimulus. But its prepared counts use Ensembl-like feature IDs and the source has no assay-specific feature map for naming MERTK or establishing that UNC106238 is a selective MerTK perturbation. It cannot be used as a MerTK perturbation bridge.

- GSE95588 has exact source-label feature-map rows for MERTK, the nine parent state/proxy genes, HBEGF, NOTCH3, JAG1/DLL1 and FLS outcome genes in both tables. The maps explicitly mark these rows `source_label_preserved_not_independently_annotated`. The coculture design has eight columns (`m_r1`, `mf_r1`, `mt_r1`, `mtf_r1`, `m_r2`, `mf_r2`, `mt_r2`, `mtf_r2`); the d1/d2/d3/d4 design has 70 P1–P4 condition columns including M, MT, MTF and compound-suffixed labels. In both designs every `donor_id` is null and `donor_status=unresolved`; the available design does not verify donor-to-GSM mapping or the biological meaning of the encoded condition strings. These tables may support a descriptive, source-internal expression audit after a mapping review, but not donor-aware validation or target-specific inference.

Therefore the child does not claim that a cross-assay perturbational bridge is available. It tests a narrower falsifiable hypothesis: after the leakage-free state-versus-contribution computation is complete, no available source-separated context contrast can upgrade the result to MerTK-mediated FLS biology unless the contrast has verified target identity, exposure semantics and functional endpoint evidence. The computable claim is limited to whether a fixed MerTK-associated expression direction is composition-resistant in the E-MTAB-8873 terminal assay and whether its pattern is compatible or incompatible with generic/context structure. Target engagement, causal signaling and FLS function remain unidentifiable.

## Hypothesis, estimand and rivals

Hypothesis H: in E-MTAB-8873, a fixed nine-marker direction derived only from macrophage-only E-MTAB-8322, and transferred only as a rank/direction proxy, retains a stable association with the terminal FLS inflammatory expression outcome after a separate macrophage-RNA contribution proxy and donor/run/composition sensitivities. H is an assay-level state-versus-composition hypothesis, not a claim that MerTK mediates the effect.

State/proxy positives are P={MERTK, CD163, MRC1, FOLR2, C1QA, C1QB, APOE}; negatives are N={SPP1, TNF}; G=P union N. The outcome-only set is O={MMP3, MMP9, IL6, IL1B, CXCL8, CCL2, ICAM1, TNFAIP3}. G∩O is empty. IL1B is excluded from every predictor, contribution proxy, reference fit and QC decision.

The strongest available evidence supports a MerTK-positive synovial macrophage state associated with remission biology and fibroblast repair in a prior study, plus assay rows that can represent a related expression direction. It does not support direct binding, selectivity, intracellular pathway activation, secretion, FLS invasion or clinical benefit.

The leading rivals are:

1. Composition/material: a high score is more macrophage RNA or a changed macrophage/FLS mixture. A contribution proxy and mixed-ratio interpolation should explain it.
2. Generic activation or LPS/context: the response is shared by macrophage activation, stress or assay context, not a resolution/MerTK direction. LPS and context controls should reproduce it.
3. Compound/off-target: the recorded inhibitor response is a pharmacologic or run effect unrelated to MerTK. The single Mneg block, paired runs and any context contrast are only bounded controls.
4. Donor/run/selection: the pattern is driven by R1/R2/R5, contributing-donor composition or the R1 donor conflict.
5. Alternative macrophage communication: HBEGF/EGFR, SPP1 or unmeasured ligands mediate FLS behavior. The targeted panel cannot adjudicate this.

An association that survives adjustment remains descriptive. It does not identify a mechanism.

All source files are read-only. No donor or specimen ID is joined across datasets, even when SA strings look similar. Derived tables and results belong in this branch.

## Computable Harbor experiment

### Stage 0: binding gate

Recheck every matrix/design one-to-one join, exact feature key and source hash. Save the full exclusion table. Fail closed if a required row or design field is absent. For E-MTAB-8322 read sparse raw matrices through gene-map row order and barcode column order. For E-MTAB-8873 preserve transcript identifiers. For GSE95588 resolve the feature-map record before naming any row; for E-MTAB-8316 retain Ensembl feature IDs without target naming. Do not use any outcome row while constructing a state, contribution or reference coordinate.

The temporal boundary is endpoint-only for E-MTAB-8873 and cross-sectional for E-MTAB-8322. E-MTAB-8316 has a recorded compound context but no verified exposure/washout timing beyond the metadata; GSE95588 has no verified timing in the bound design. No transition, persistence or treatment-response trajectory may be claimed.

### Stage 1: primary baseline

Normalize each relevant prepared sample with x_ig=log(1+10^6 c_ig/L_i), standardizing within the prespecified source/analysis unit. In E-MTAB-8322 calculate S9 from P and N. In E-MTAB-8873 calculate S9 and the contribution proxy A9=mean of the nine G rows, then construct Y=mean of the eight outcome rows only after all predictor choices are frozen. Report library size, detected features, recorded cells, run, FLS donor component, contributing-donor string and all design labels.

The baseline estimand is the fixed-score state-versus-contribution comparison, not an unadjusted Mpos/Mneg treatment effect. Report paired deltas in Y, S9 and A9 for the three usable Mpos blocks; report the single R1 Mneg interaction as one bounded block contrast; compare mixed-ratio samples with a predeclared 1:3 or 3:1 convex prediction using the closest same-run/pure controls. Use block/donor-mixture resampling, leave-one-run-out sensitivity and no asymptotic p-value from three Mpos blocks plus one Mneg block.

### Stage 2: substantive alternative on the same inputs

Fit a constrained reference projection using only the same nine G rows. In E-MTAB-8322 construct high-S9 and low-S9 macrophage endmembers from prespecified S9 quartiles, with leave-one-verified-donor-out versions. In E-MTAB-8873 include FLS-only records as a measured nine-row background reference. For each endpoint sample fit nonnegative library-scaled reconstruction with m_i (macrophage RNA contribution) and q_i in [0,1] (coordinate between low- and high-S9 macrophage endmembers). The fitting target is G reconstruction only; do not use Y, inhibitor labels, condition labels or outcome rows in fitting.

Use leave-one-run-out across R1/R2/R5 and leave-one-mixed-ratio-out checks. Evaluate held-out nine-row reconstruction error, pure/mixed ratio ordering, m/q stability, q–S9 agreement, and the post-fit Y association after m. Compare baseline and alternative on the same Y, S9, A9, block deltas, mixed-ratio residuals and block-aware uncertainty. This alternative could reveal whether nominally high S9 is mostly more macrophage RNA or a changed state coordinate, which the fixed score loses. Defer it if m and q are non-identifiable, FLS-only controls cannot be reconstructed, endmembers are donor-unstable, or known pure/mixed ordering fails.

Compute estimate: managed CPU job, approximately 16 CPUs and 32–64 GiB, within the configured discovery/solver planning envelope; no GPU is needed because the bound endpoint matrix is 33×445 and the alternative uses nine-row references. This is an estimate, not a measured fit. The only executed job was the 2-CPU, 4-GiB, 4.54-second schema/mapping audit `job-c954bfd7492602a48269c4bb`. No biological fit or model result is claimed.

### Stage 3: orthogonal-source deferral gate

Do not pool or join any source identities. After Stage 1–2 are frozen, the solver may produce a separate table labeled `context_audit`:

- E-MTAB-8316: report only source-internal paired metadata counts and, if an expert first supplies an assay feature map and compound identity/selectivity, a donor-cluster-averaged descriptive response. In the current package, target-specific analysis is blocked.
- GSE95588: report only row availability, condition-string inventory, and optional source-internal descriptive expression contrasts after feature-map review. Because all donor mappings are unresolved, no donor-aware uncertainty, independent validation or target-specific perturbation conclusion is permitted.

These context audits cannot change S9/A9/Y, cannot provide a reference fit, and cannot upgrade the primary conclusion. A positive expression pattern in GSE95588 is compatible with a MerTK-associated proxy, but cannot establish target engagement or mechanism.

## Falsification and interpretation

Support for the computable hypothesis requires all of the following: S9 direction is stable in donor-held-out E-MTAB-8322 summaries; S9 and A9 are not effectively collinear; q agrees with S9 while m does not fully explain Y; the paired Mpos pattern remains after A9/m and QC sensitivity; mixed-ratio residuals do not follow composition interpolation; LPS controls do not reproduce it; the single Mneg block does not erase the pattern; and the projection is stable under leave-one-run/block-out. This supports a composition-resistant MerTK-associated expression direction in this endpoint assay and justifies the smallest orthogonal engagement study. It does not support MerTK binding, selectivity, phosphorylation, secretion, FLS function or clinical benefit.

Adverse evidence is a score instability, near-collinearity, mixed-ratio interpolation, loss after A9/m adjustment, inhibitor changing m rather than q, Mneg/LPS reproduction, one-run dependence, or projection instability. This falsifies the composition-resistant interpretation for this assay and redirects work toward composition, generic activation, alternative macrophage communication or compound pharmacology. It does not show MerTK is irrelevant in RA.

Inconclusive evidence is a missing/ambiguous feature or join, unstable endmembers, unresolved contributing-donor structure, failure of m/q identification, sparse target rows, or uncertainty dominated by one block. A calculable score without target engagement or validated cell-fraction meaning is inconclusive for mechanism.

The verifier can check paths/hashes, row maps, joins, disjoint feature sets, exclusions, normalization, predictor-blind fitting, reconstruction, contrasts, resampling and whether the reported classification follows those outputs. It cannot adjudicate MerTK occupancy, inhibitor selectivity, downstream signaling, actual macrophage fraction, secretion, FLS invasion, matrix degradation, spatial localization, flare or patient benefit.

## Smallest expert-ready follow-up

If the computable pattern is supportive, use new independent human synovial macrophage donors and matched FLS, keeping donor identities explicit. The minimal factorial should include vehicle, a MerTK-selective perturbation with documented exposure, and an orthogonal MerTK loss-of-function or blocking reagent, plus a non-targeting/inactive control. Record baseline, exposure, washout and terminal times; include viability.

The first mechanistic endpoint must be direct target engagement: surface MerTK abundance plus ligand-stimulated MerTK phosphorylation/occupancy (or a validated cellular target-engagement assay), with a concentration/selectivity panel. The same macrophage–FLS preparations then measure secreted IL-6, IL-1β, CXCL8, CCL2, MMP3/MMP9 and a prespecified FLS invasion or matrix-degradation assay. A MerTK-specific mechanism requires concordant engagement loss and functional reversal under both orthogonal perturbations, not merely a transcript change. Include HBEGF/EGFR and SPP1/IL1B measurements as rival-mechanism controls. Without this target-engagement and functional evidence, the current study must remain an expression/state-proxy study.

## Alternatives and revisit criteria

The fixed nine-marker score is the simple baseline: transparent, no learned weights, same G inputs and explicit state-versus-contribution estimand. It loses distributed information and cannot itself identify m versus q.

The constrained nine-row reference projection is the substantive alternative: same inputs, fitting target G, donor-held-out endmember construction, leave-run-out split, held-out reconstruction and block-aware uncertainty. It adds information about contribution versus state coordinate but is deferred if the coordinates are not identifiable. It is not selected because it is more complex; it is selected conditionally because it addresses the scientific rival the baseline cannot.

An unrestricted latent or neural model is not chosen. The reason is not CPU/GPU ideology: 33 endpoint samples, one Mneg block, and absent target engagement would not resolve the mechanistic uncertainty. Revisit only with more independent donors and orthogonal molecular/functional endpoints.

A pooled cross-assay perturbation model is explicitly not chosen because the source namespaces, feature annotation and donor mappings do not support the required identity and target joins. Revisit if E-MTAB-8316 receives a verified feature map plus compound-selectivity/protocol evidence, or if GSE95588 receives verified GSM-to-donor/condition mappings and independent donor structure. A ligand/receptor or mediation model is deferred until direct ligand/protein, secretion and functional FLS measurements exist.

## Actual scientific deliverable
